error_codes.description: The host has addresses only in an IP family the Session holds no local address of, such as IPv6 addresses for a Session bound to an IPv4 address. Add a local address of that family to the run's local addresses, or reach the host another way.
error_codes.name: address_family_unavailable

error_codes.description: A pinned download the call needed failed: the network, an HTTP status, or bytes whose digest is not the pinned one. Retry, or install beforehand with the Product's `browser install`, or point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache.
error_codes.name: artifact_download_failed

error_codes.description: The `offline` setting refused a pinned download the call needed. Run the Product's `browser install` beforehand where the cache is writable, point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache, or lift `offline` where it was set.
error_codes.name: artifact_unavailable_offline

error_codes.description: The call names an attempt that already ended: its handler returned, it failed or was skipped, its lease ended, or its Run stopped. Nothing it asked for was done, so a forgotten `await` never silently loses a link.
error_codes.name: attempt_ended

error_codes.description: The site refused the document a navigation reached with a Block cause the engine cannot get past, such as a rate limit, an IP block or a challenge: raised by the call that waited for that navigation, or else by the page's next call. The Session stays open with its cookies, never replaced, and nothing waits on the site's `Retry-After`: the program decides whether to wait, open another Session or pause for a person. The details name the cause, the URL, the status and `retry_after`, the time the site asked for or `null`.
error_codes.name: blocked

error_codes.description: The Run's folder holds no body of this ID: the Run or the body is unknown, or the ID is not a body's.
error_codes.name: body_not_found

error_codes.description: The browser no longer holds the response's body, as after the page navigated away or once its buffer evicted it, or the response has none, as a redirect's: the engine keeps a body only for a response obtained through `page.wait_for_request_finished`, `route.fetch` or `page.request`, which the fix names. Where Playwright and Puppeteer say "Request content was evicted from inspector cache". A retry finds the body gone all the same.
error_codes.name: body_unavailable

error_codes.description: The Browser host the engine reached is of a version this engine cannot drive. Upgrade the Browser host, which either Product's executable runs as its `browser-host` command.
error_codes.name: browser_host_outdated

error_codes.description: The browser's build is installed, but it did not start or did not open the page: it exited, or its connection refused or fell silent. The details name its executable and how it ended.
error_codes.name: browser_launch_failed

error_codes.description: The browser build a launch needs is not in the Browser cache and the engine cannot write that cache, such as an image's read-only `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH`; or a browser named by channel or path is not there. Run the Product's `browser install` where the cache is writable, install the browser of that channel, or correct the path.
error_codes.name: browser_not_installed

error_codes.description: A handler's call on a page its forced fetch tier serves from a document, which that tier cannot serve exactly, such as a click, `evaluate` or a wait for content the document lacks: under a forced tier nothing escalates to the browser. The details name `fetch.tier`, the tier, the Label that forced it when one did, and the call; the fix names `fetch.tier: auto` or `browser`, and for a wait also content the page may simply lack. A request's own document that declares no encoding and is not UTF-8, which only the browser's guess reads, fails the same way under a forced tier (ADR 0119), its call `fetch.encoding` and its fix naming `fetch.encoding` and `fetch.tier`.
error_codes.name: browser_required

error_codes.description: Chromium's sandbox cannot start on this host, so the engine launches no browser. `environment` names what refuses it (Docker's or containerd's default seccomp profile, Kubernetes' `RuntimeDefault`, Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction on unprivileged user namespaces, or `unknown` for a refusal the probe does not recognise, which the message names), and `fix` the fix; an Operator policy may instead switch `security.browser_sandbox` off, which the run reports.
error_codes.name: browser_sandbox_unavailable

error_codes.description: The call was stopped in flight, at its next cancellation point: its Client sent `$/cancel`, or what it needed was closed under it.
error_codes.name: call_cancelled

error_codes.description: A capability this engine cannot provide where a setting asks for it, such as a Session opening from a Session source of a kind this engine does not read: the details name the setting, the layer that set it and what it asked for, and its fix names the value that does without it.
error_codes.name: capability_unavailable

error_codes.description: A `cdp_url` Session source names an address ADR 0056's rules refuse, before any connection: a private address from a value that is not Operator-configured, loopback from a Client acting for a model (its project configuration included) or a Recipe, or a private address under `egress.no_private_endpoints`. The details name the address without its query or credentials, the settings layer that gave it, the rule, the address it resolved to and the fix: set the address in Operator policy or in user configuration, or give a public address.
error_codes.name: cdp_url_not_allowed

error_codes.description: A pinned host presented a certificate whose public key is not its pin, or its pin row cannot be read, so nothing was sent to it, nor is for the rest of the run. The details carry the host, both SHA-256 hashes and the fix: a person accepts the new key with `certs accept` in an interactive prompt or the Console, which no agent, Recipe or `--json` command can do.
error_codes.name: certificate_changed

error_codes.description: A host's certificate failed verification and no exception covers its domain, so nothing was sent to it. The details name the host, the failure (`expired`, `not_yet_valid`, `unknown_issuer`, `name_mismatch`, `self_signed`, `revoked`, or another failure as text) and, in `fix`, the setting that makes an exception for that domain.
error_codes.name: certificate_invalid

error_codes.description: The Connection the attempt's request went on ended before its handler answered: the program or one of its `workers=N` handler processes ended, or its Connection dropped. Not the handler's own failure (`handler_failed`): the attempt committed nothing and is retried, on another Connection that serves the crawl, under `crawl.retry.max`.
error_codes.name: client_gone

error_codes.description: The call was made on a value its program had closed: a Connection, or a Run, Session or Page under it. A value never reopens: connect again, or start the Run again by its Run ID.
error_codes.name: closed

error_codes.description: The Connection to the engine dropped before the call was answered, so whether it took effect is unknown. The Client connects again by itself; make the call again once it has, after checking that an Effect did not happen.
error_codes.name: connection_lost

error_codes.description: The Console did not start: another program holds the port of `console.address`. The Daemon still serves its Clients. Stop the other program, or set `console.address` to a free port (port 0 takes any free one) and restart the Daemon.
error_codes.name: console_port_in_use

error_codes.description: The foreground Daemon is draining on `SIGTERM`: it takes no run and checkpoints every live run as resumable, then exits. Start or resume the run on the Daemon that replaces it.
error_codes.name: daemon_draining

error_codes.description: No Daemon could be reached, so nothing was called: nothing answers where `GOODFETCH_URL` or its runtime file says it listens, it closed the Connection before it answered `hello`, as one does for a wrong `GOODFETCH_TOKEN`, it went away while the command connected, or its files cannot be read or its major's pick cannot be started. The message says which, and the `fix` what to do.
error_codes.name: daemon_unreachable

error_codes.description: The crawl declares a second Dataset of a name it already declares, so it was not started. The details name the Dataset. Give each Dataset its own name.
error_codes.name: dataset_duplicate

error_codes.description: A Dataset's key names a field that is no top-level field its JSON Schema requires, so a Record could lack it and the crawl was not started (`reason` `not_required`, naming the field); or a start under the ID of a Run changes the key of a Dataset that holds Records, so the Run did no work and a Sink's upsert never mixes two identities (`reason` `changed`, naming both keys). The details name the Dataset. Key a Dataset only by fields its schema requires, and keep its key for the Run's life or start a new Run.
error_codes.name: dataset_key_invalid

error_codes.description: A Record was pushed into a Dataset the crawl does not declare, such as another crawl's, so it was not staged; `run.records` read such a Dataset, so nothing was read; or a start under the ID of a Run whose Dataset holds Records no longer declares it, a renamed one included, so the Run did no work and no Record is orphaned. The details name the Dataset and those the crawl declares. Declare the Dataset again, or start a new Run.
error_codes.name: dataset_unknown

error_codes.description: The call's deadline passed before what it waited for came, such as a response's first byte or a navigation. Its `limit` names the timeout's setting, its value and the layer that set it: raise that setting, or wait for the right thing.
error_codes.name: deadline_exceeded

error_codes.description: The dialog was answered already, by an earlier `accept` or `dismiss`, or it closed, its handler having ended or the dialog having got its default: the first answer stands and this one changed nothing.
error_codes.name: dialog_already_handled

error_codes.description: The call would stage an output with its attempt (an enqueue, a seed added through `ctx.run`, a Record or a Key-value store write through `ctx.run`) while a declared Effect's body runs in that attempt. A re-run that finds the Effect in the Effect journal does not run the body again, so the output would be lost for good; nothing was staged. The details' `fix` says to stage it after the declaration, from the output the body returned.
error_codes.name: effect_staging_refused

error_codes.description: The run's egress policy refused a request before it connected: a host the domain policy does not allow, an address that is not globally reachable, or a scheme no request may use. The details name the URL, the rule, the address when there is one and the setting that would allow it.
error_codes.name: egress_refused

error_codes.description: The Attached engine ended before its Connection was closed, so the call has no answer. Its details carry the exit code or signal and the last 64 KiB of its stderr.
error_codes.name: engine_exited

error_codes.description: `connect()` found no engine executable to start: the Product's engine-path variable names no executable, or the Product's platform package is not installed. The `fix` names the variable or the package.
error_codes.name: engine_not_found

error_codes.description: The engine wrote a line that is not one JSON-RPC message on the Connection, such as a log line on an Attached engine's stdout, so the Client ended the Connection. A bug in Goodfetch: report it with the line its details carry.
error_codes.name: engine_output_invalid

error_codes.description: Windows refused to start the file: Smart App Control, or another App Control policy, blocks executables without a signature or reputation it trusts. Goodfetch never re-signs a file it did not build. For a browser, use the Goodfetch Chromium or an installed Chrome by channel; otherwise turn Smart App Control off, or ask the device's administrator to allow the file.
error_codes.name: executable_blocked_by_smart_app_control

error_codes.description: The bytes of a file could not be written: no space or quota left, or an I/O error, or any failure where the engine keeps its files. No partial file is left. Free space where the files go, or ask the Daemon's operator, then make the same call again.
error_codes.name: file_write_failed

error_codes.description: A file, such as a run state or a Checkpoint, is of a format version this engine cannot read: a newer minor or major, written by a newer engine, which `fix` says to upgrade to, or an older major, which `upgrade-files` upgrades. The file is left as it is.
error_codes.name: format_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: The program's handler failed with its own error, such as an exception; the attempt committed nothing. It is retried only when `crawl.retry.handler_failed` is on, since a bug fails the same way every time.
error_codes.name: handler_failed

error_codes.description: The attempt's lease ended with no answer from the program's handler: its process ended, its Connection dropped, or it hung. The attempt committed nothing and counts against `crawl.retry.max`.
error_codes.name: handler_lost

error_codes.description: A header value the engine would send holds a CR, an LF or a NUL, which could end the header and start another, so it is refused before it reaches the wire or the browser. The details name the header and the character, never the value. Remove the character from the value.
error_codes.name: header_value_invalid

error_codes.description: A bug in Goodfetch: an object such as a Session or a page received an event its state cannot receive. Report it with the object, the state and the event its details carry.
error_codes.name: internal

error_codes.description: The attempt's lease ended before it committed: its handler answered after the lease's end, or the run file holds a later lease of its work item. Its outputs are discarded, and the commit of the work item's next attempt is the one that counts.
error_codes.name: lease_lost

error_codes.description: A newer engine wrote a Limit this engine cannot evaluate, and it may cover the run; the details name it. Upgrade the engine.
error_codes.name: limit_not_understood

error_codes.description: A Limit that covers the run has nothing left in its period; the details name its scope, its Usage kind, its period and when it starts again. Wait for the next period, or ask a person to raise it.
error_codes.name: limit_reached

error_codes.description: `egress.local_addresses` yields no address this host can send from: a listed address the host does not hold, an interface it does not have or that holds no address, or an IPv6 prefix with none of the host's addresses in it and, on Linux, not routed locally with `net.ipv6.ip_nonlocal_bind` on; or a Session whose browser this engine does not launch on this machine (a Borrowed browser, a third-party CDP browser, a Browser host's) or whose `https://` proxy the egress relay does not chain through. The binding is never ignored: assign the address, correct the value, route the prefix to the host, or open the Session on a browser the engine launches here.
error_codes.name: local_address_unavailable

error_codes.description: The document the navigation reached is a login page, even one answered with a 200: the Session's login is lost, judged by its Page check's `login_page`, or by the built-in detector when it declares none. The page stays on the login page, the Session open with its cookies. The details name the URL, the status and what judged it.
error_codes.name: logged_out

error_codes.description: The engine's own resolver got no usable answer for the host name: its name servers timed out, refused the query, failed or could not be reached. Check the name servers of the system's resolver configuration, or map the name with the `resolve` setting.
error_codes.name: name_lookup_failed

error_codes.description: The resolver found no address for the host name. The engine's own resolver, used on Linux and for Sessions with a local address, reads the system's resolver configuration and hosts file but asks neither NSS modules (such as a directory service or a VPN client's) nor multicast DNS, so a name only they resolve, such as a `.local` name, fails here. Map such a name to its address with the `resolve` setting, or correct the name.
error_codes.name: name_not_resolved

error_codes.description: The navigation reached no document: the browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, is in the details, or the browser failed it for a reason it did not name.
error_codes.name: navigation_failed

error_codes.description: Another navigation of the page started before this one committed, so this one reached no document: the page went where the other took it.
error_codes.name: navigation_interrupted

error_codes.description: The call asks a Daemon about itself, and this engine is an Attached engine. Ask the Daemon of the major, found through its runtime file, or run `daemon status`.
error_codes.name: not_a_daemon

error_codes.description: The running engine's Product does not carry what was asked: a Client that needs Foxhound reached a Collie engine, or a call, a setting or a value only Foxhound carries reached one. Run it with Foxhound, which contains everything Collie does, or connect to a Foxhound engine.
error_codes.name: not_in_product

error_codes.description: The document the navigation reached is neither the expected page nor the login page of its Session's Page check, `session.page_check`, whatever its HTTP status: a page the program did not mean to reach, such as an error page or a layout the site changed. The page stays on that document. The details name its URL and status.
error_codes.name: page_check_failed

error_codes.description: The page's renderer crashed, or its browser process was lost while the call ran; `browser_exit` says how the browser ended when it is what was lost. The page is gone: open another.
error_codes.name: page_crashed

error_codes.description: Some of a page's events are lost. Either the engine fell too far behind the browser's events of a page that is still open and stopped reading them: the page's `page.on` listeners, waits and `response.body` reads raise this rather than answer from missing events, and the Run trace records it, while the page's other calls still work; open another page to follow its events. Or one `page.on` call's Client took too few of its events, granting too few credits, so 1,024 waited unsent: that call raises this once it sent them; listen again and grant credits as events are read.
error_codes.name: page_events_lost

error_codes.description: A page function threw in the page, or did not parse, or is an expression given an argument, which only a function takes. The details give the error's name, its message and the page's stack. A page function sees only the page and its one argument, never the program's variables, so a `ReferenceError`'s fix names the argument: pass the value in it.
error_codes.name: page_function_failed

error_codes.description: A handler the program gave a page failed, such as a route's handler that threw: its request was aborted unless it was answered already, never sent half-changed, and its route was removed; a dialog handler's dialog got its default and the handler was removed. Raised by the call that waited on that request, such as the `goto` whose document it was, or by the call the dialog blocked, or else by the next call on its page. The details name the handler, the URL of the request or of the dialog's document, and what the failure said.
error_codes.name: page_handler_failed

error_codes.description: Memory was critical and the page held more than `governor.browser.page_memory_cap`, so the Resource governor ended it once no call on it was in flight. The page is gone: open another and try again, which the governor admits once memory frees up.
error_codes.name: page_memory_exceeded

error_codes.description: A page function's result, or its argument, holds a value outside JSON, such as a DOM node, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a function, a `Map`, a `BigInt` or a cycle, which Playwright would have turned into `undefined`, silently. The details name the first such value's path from `$`, its kind and the fix: return the JSON the program needs, such as an element's text or attribute instead of the element.
error_codes.name: page_value_invalid

error_codes.description: The path the program chose cannot be written for a reason the path causes: permission denied, a read-only filesystem, a folder at the path, a file where a parent folder should be, a name the filesystem refuses, a file too large for that filesystem, or a path not found once its parents are made. No partial file is left. Change the path.
error_codes.name: path_not_writable

error_codes.description: A name or path from outside input would leave the folder the engine writes it in, or is no safe file name on Linux, macOS or Windows: a `..` or `.` part, an absolute, drive, UNC, verbatim or device path, a name Windows reserves for a device, an alternate data stream, a character Windows forbids or a control character, a trailing dot or space, a part longer than 255 bytes, an empty part or a name that is not in Unicode's composed form. It is refused on every OS alike. The details name it and its hazard.
error_codes.name: path_unsafe

error_codes.description: A URL pattern the engine cannot match: a regular expression with look-around, a back-reference or another construct outside the `regex` crate's syntax, or a glob with nested or unmatched braces. The details name the construct; match the URL with a predicate instead, which runs in the program.
error_codes.name: pattern_unsupported

error_codes.description: A crawl request's Payload was refused when it was enqueued, as a seed, an added seed or a handler's enqueue: it does not fit its Label's JSON Schema, each issue named by its path, or its JSON is longer than `crawl.payload.max_size`, which `limit` names. Nothing was added. Large content goes to the Key-value store, and the Payload carries its key.
error_codes.name: payload_invalid

error_codes.description: The crawl now declares a Label's Payload JSON Schema that the Run did not begin with, and Payloads of that Label's pending requests fail it, so the Run was not resumed and did no work. The details name the Label, how many pending Payloads fail out of how many, and the first failure. Give the new field a default in the schema, or start a new Run: a Payload is never migrated silently.
error_codes.name: payload_schema_changed

error_codes.description: Only a person gives this answer, in the Console or an interactive CLI prompt: no agent surface, SDK, script or command run under `--json` or without a terminal may. Answer it in the Console, or run the command in a terminal.
error_codes.name: person_required

error_codes.description: The Operator policy's digest changed since it was read, as by a hand edit, so nothing was written; `fix` says to read it again.
error_codes.name: policy_conflict

error_codes.description: The engine does not speak the protocol version the Client's `hello` names: it accepts its own major with the same or an older minor. Upgrade the older side.
error_codes.name: protocol_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: The Session's proxy answered `407 Proxy Authentication Required`: the Session gave it no credentials, or it refused those of `proxy.username` and `proxy.password`. The details name the proxy and the username, never the password. Fix the credentials; retrying with the same ones fails the same way.
error_codes.name: proxy_auth_failed

error_codes.description: The Session's Proxy provider answered through its proxy with a failure of its own: its traffic quota or balance is spent (`quota_exhausted`), the Session's sticky exit is gone (`sticky_session_expired`), or a failure Goodfetch does not recognize (`unrecognized`, whose text is logged, never returned). The details name the provider, the proxy and the failure, never the credentials. A provider's refusal of the credentials is `proxy_auth_failed` instead. Retry later, or open a new Session for a new exit.
error_codes.name: proxy_provider_unavailable

error_codes.description: The engine could not open the loopback relay a Session's proxy goes through, such as when the machine has no free local port: the proxy itself was never tried. The details name the proxy, never its credentials, and the local error. Retry once the machine frees ports or file descriptors.
error_codes.name: proxy_relay_unavailable

error_codes.description: The Session's proxy could not be reached, its TLS failed, or it refused the tunnel or the request with an error of its own: the details name the proxy, never its credentials, and the browser's network error when it named one. It is the proxy's failure, never the site's and never `navigation_failed`: retry later, or through another proxy.
error_codes.name: proxy_unavailable

error_codes.description: The query failed in a way the engine does not recognise, such as a run file it could not read; the engine's log holds the cause. Try again; if it fails the same way, report it with the log.
error_codes.name: query_failed

error_codes.description: The SQL tab did not run the statement: it does not parse, names a table, column or function that does not exist or a run the query did not select, is not one `SELECT` or `WITH` statement (a write, `ATTACH`, `INSTALL`, `LOAD` or `COPY`), or reads a file or URL, which the SQL tab never reaches. The details say which. Read only the selected runs' tables, and select the run first.
error_codes.name: query_invalid

error_codes.description: The query needed more memory than `dataset.query.memory_limit`, so it was stopped. The details name the setting, its value and its layer. Aggregate or filter sooner, select fewer runs, or raise `dataset.query.memory_limit`.
error_codes.name: query_memory_exceeded

error_codes.description: A Record is no JSON object, fails its Dataset's JSON Schema, or lacks a field of its Dataset's key, so it was not staged. The details name the Dataset and each issue by its path, a JSON Pointer into the Record. Caught in the handler, the attempt keeps its other outputs; escaping it, the request ends `failed` and is not retried, since the same Record fails the same way.
error_codes.name: record_invalid

error_codes.description: The engine ran out of memory or storage for the Run: it checkpointed and stopped it, or refused to start it where its run file would go. The details name the `resource`. Resume it once memory or space frees up, on an engine with a larger allowance, or with lower ceilings.
error_codes.name: resources_exhausted

error_codes.description: A body or JSON the engine read from outside passed one of its limits, so the engine stopped reading it: more decoded bytes than `network.max_body_size`, more decoded bytes per received byte than `network.max_decompression_ratio` once past 1 MiB, or JSON nested deeper than `network.max_json_depth`. The details name the URL, the setting and its value; raise the setting for a site you trust.
error_codes.name: response_limit_exceeded

error_codes.description: A handler's call that reads, waits on or acts on the document of a page whose accepted response is not an HTML document, such as a PDF its Label's `crawl.content_types` lists: a locator, `content()`, `formats`, `evaluate`, a screenshot or an AI verb. It fails at once on every tier and never escalates. The details name the response's content type and the call; the fix names `ctx.response`, which holds the body.
error_codes.name: response_not_document

error_codes.description: The response is not one a handler is handed: a 3xx that is not one of Fetch's redirect statuses (301, 302, 303, 307, 308), or a redirect whose `Location` is missing, does not parse or names no HTTP(S) URL. The details name the response's `url` and `status`, and a `fix` naming `crawl.handle_statuses`, which hands a status to the handler. A sitemap seed's sitemap (ADR 0093) fails with it on any status but a 2xx, 408, 429 or 5xx, and on a file that is no sitemap the crawl reads: XML that breaks off, another root, a gzip stream that does not decode, or more than sitemaps.org's 50,000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed; its `details` name the `url`, and the `status` when one answered. Not retried: the site answers the same again.
error_codes.name: response_not_ok

error_codes.description: The response's body broke off before its end: shorter than its `Content-Length`, a chunked body without its last chunk, or a stream the server or the connection ended. A navigation waiting for `domcontentloaded` or `load` raises it for its main document; one that answered at `commit` leaves it to the body's read. The details name the URL and the bytes received and expected.
error_codes.name: response_truncated

error_codes.description: The site is failing for now: its 5xx or 408 response stayed after the retries ran out, or its `Retry-After` asked for a time further away than `politeness.retry_after.max`, so nothing is sent to its domain before then and nothing waits for it. The details name the response's `status` (`null` for a request held unsent), the time the site asked for as `retry_after` when it asked, and a `fix`. `run.retry_failed` re-admits the request once the site is back.
error_codes.name: response_unavailable

error_codes.description: The route's request was answered already, by an earlier `continue`, `fulfill`, `abort` or `fallback`, or its handler ended: the first answer stands and this one changed nothing.
error_codes.name: route_already_handled

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, and the owner the Run index names did not take the action: it did not answer, or does not own the Run. The engine retried the lock 5 times over about a second; the writer may end, so try again later.
error_codes.name: run_busy

error_codes.description: The Run ID names a Run started with other inputs, or by another caller; the details list each difference. Start under another Run ID.
error_codes.name: run_conflict

error_codes.description: The Run ended `finished`, so it takes no new work, such as a page or a Session it would open: start a Run under a new Run ID. The details name the Run.
error_codes.name: run_ended

error_codes.description: The Run ID is not one the engine takes: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 128, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.
error_codes.name: run_id_invalid

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, so this one cannot write the Run; the other may end.
error_codes.name: run_in_use

error_codes.description: The Run has no live writer and has not ended, as after a crash, so it has no report and none comes: a start with its Run ID resumes it. The details name the Run.
error_codes.name: run_interrupted

error_codes.description: A resumed Run's data key does not open under the key-encryption key `run_state.key_reference` names, such as a Checkpoint moved to a machine whose own key is another: the key that wrapped it never travels with the Checkpoint. The details name the Run, the setting, the reference resolved and the reference that wrapped the key, never a value. Name the key that wrapped it, in project configuration or configuration, and resume again.
error_codes.name: run_key_mismatch

error_codes.description: The engine still runs the Run, so it cannot be discarded: stop it first with `run.stop` or `run.abort`, or let it finish, then discard it. The details name the Run.
error_codes.name: run_live

error_codes.description: No Run has this Run ID: the Run index does not list it.
error_codes.name: run_not_found

error_codes.description: The action was forwarded to this engine as the Run's owner, and this engine does not own the Run: the Run index named an engine that has since ended or restarted. The engine that forwarded it retries the Run's writer lock.
error_codes.name: run_not_owned

error_codes.description: The Run's state is missing, damaged or cannot be written at its location; the details give the path. The engine never starts afresh under that Run ID.
error_codes.name: run_state_unavailable

error_codes.description: The sample crawl refused its pages.
error_codes.name: sample_crawl_refused

error_codes.description: The sample operation refused the text.
error_codes.name: sample_refused

error_codes.description: A Secret placeholder's value would go to a domain outside its binding's `domains`: the field's frame or the request's URL. The details name the placeholder, the reference and the domain, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_domain_not_allowed

error_codes.description: A Secret placeholder's value would be typed or sent where other code may read it, or to a host reached through an invalid-certificate exception, so it was not resolved. The details name the placeholder, the reference, the domain and the `reason`, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_input_refused

error_codes.description: A Secret provider gave no value for a reference: a missing variable, a locked keychain, an unreachable vault, the caller's `resolveSecret` missing or throwing, no answer within `timeout.secret`. `failure` says which, and the details name the placeholder or setting, the reference and the provider, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_unavailable

error_codes.description: No scope binds the Secret placeholder a call names. `bound` lists the placeholders bound, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_unbound

error_codes.description: The Run is bound to the machine its Session source is on, and this is another machine: its login would reach sites from a new IP under the same cookies. Resume it on its own machine, or serve its Session source through a Browser host.
error_codes.name: session_bound_to_machine

error_codes.description: A value of the wrong type or out of the setting's own range, an empty or unparsable deployment variable, or a settings file that does not parse.
error_codes.name: setting_invalid

error_codes.description: A value a lower layer locked or capped, outside a Recipe's exposed bounds, or one only a lower layer may set or widen, such as `tls.trusted_cas` from a run. `limit` names the setting and the layer that holds it.
error_codes.name: setting_locked

error_codes.description: A setting given where it cannot take effect: in a layer that may not hold it, such as `browser_cache.max_unused_age` outside user configuration and an Operator policy, or on a Run it does not apply to, such as a crawl's setting on a Collie Run.
error_codes.name: setting_not_applicable

error_codes.description: A key no Product knows, or an unknown `GOODFETCH_` variable. The message names the closest valid one.
error_codes.name: setting_unknown

error_codes.description: The site's preferences refused the navigation or the request before it left, or refused the document once its response arrived, leaving the page on a blank document: its robots.txt disallows the URL (`robots_txt`), its `Crawl-delay` asks for more than the crawl allows (`crawl_delay`), or a use signal it sends refuses the crawl's Purpose (`use_signals`). Only a crawl handler's page asks a site's preferences; a page a program opens never raises it. The details name the URL and the reason.
error_codes.name: site_preferences_refused

error_codes.description: The call would stage one more admission (an enqueue, an `enqueueLinks` call or a seed added through `ctx.run`) with an attempt that already staged `crawl.max_staged_enqueues` of them, which the attempt holds in the engine's memory until it commits. Nothing was staged. Enqueue many links with one `enqueueLinks` call, or raise the setting, which `limit` names.
error_codes.name: staging_full

error_codes.description: The locator still matched several elements when the action's timeout passed, so the action did nothing. The details list every match, each with a locator that reaches it alone, and `limit` names the timeout's setting; a longer timeout would not fix the locator.
error_codes.name: target_not_unique

error_codes.description: The navigation followed as many redirects as it may and was redirected again, as a redirect loop is: the browser's count is 20 requests in a navigation's chain, its first included, so Chromium follows 19 redirects. The details name the first URL, the hops followed and the count. A retry meets the same chain.
error_codes.name: too_many_redirects

error_codes.description: `upgrade-files` does not upgrade from this major: one this release's upgrade paths do not list, whose message names the release to upgrade through first, or a newer major than the executable's, whose message says to upgrade. No file is changed.
error_codes.name: upgrade_source_unsupported

error_codes.description: The Key-value store refused the key or its value: a key must be 1 to 512 Unicode scalar values with no control character, and a value any JSON but null, which `get` answers for an absent key; remove a key with `delete`. Bytes are read with `getBytes` and JSON with `get`, never the other way. The details name the key and say which was refused.
error_codes.name: value_invalid

error_groups.name: program

error_groups.description: A policy, a Limit, a lock or a person refused. Change a setting, raise the Limit or ask the operator.

events.description: A Pinned artifact the call needs is downloading into the Browser cache: the bytes received so far, out of those announced.
events.name: browser_cache.download_progress

events.description: The engine's Resource governor sampled: its Memory allowance and what set it, the memory the engine and its children use, the host's pressure, CPU and Tokio saturation, its level and what holds it there, and each kind's concurrency. Telemetry: a newer sample replaces an unsent one.
events.name: engine.system_info

events.description: The engine no longer holds the position the subscription resumes after: the events since are gone, and this gives the current state, every live Run's axes and every item of "Needs you", from which the stream continues.
events.name: events.resync

events.description: An item of "Needs you" appeared, changed or left the list: resolved, by a person or by its Run, or dismissed. Lossless: a subscription that falls behind next takes `events.resync`, which holds every item.
events.name: needs_you.changed

events.description: The page closed: the engine closed it, or its window was closed in the browser outside every Client. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `close`, just before that call answers.
events.name: page.close

events.description: The page wrote a message to its console, `ConsoleMessage`: its type, text and location. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `console`, the only time the engine reads the page's console.
events.name: page.console

events.description: The page crashed: its renderer, or its browser's process, which exited abnormally. Its calls in flight raised `page_crashed`, and so does each later call. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `crash`.
events.name: page.crash

events.description: The document of the page's main frame fired `DOMContentLoaded`. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `dom_content_loaded`.
events.name: page.dom_content_loaded

events.description: A navigation of the page reached a file the browser downloads instead of showing, such as a PDF: the navigation answers no response and the page keeps its document. Names the page, the file's URL and the name the browser suggests.
events.name: page.download

events.description: The document of the page's main frame fired `load`. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `load`.
events.name: page.load

events.description: An exception the page did not catch, `WebError`: its name, message and stack. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `page_error`.
events.name: page.page_error

events.description: The page opened a popup, `window.open()` or a link opening another window: a page of the same Session, already under its routes and its interception, published before the popup's first request leaves. Published while `page.on` listens to `popup`.
events.name: page.popup

events.description: The page sent a request, `Request`, once per hop of a redirect chain: its URL, method, headers, body, resource type, navigation flag and the hops before it. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `request`; a service worker's own requests are never a page's.
events.name: page.request

events.description: A request of the page failed, `Request` with its `failure`, as Playwright reports one: the browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_FAILED` for one a route aborted or `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, and the Error code when the engine blocked it, such as `egress_refused`, so a refusal is never a timeout. A response whose body broke off fails too. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `request_failed`; the Run trace records each request the engine refused that no call waited on.
events.name: page.request_failed

events.description: A request of the page got its whole response, its body included. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `request_finished`.
events.name: page.request_finished

events.description: A request of the page got its response's head: the request and its response, whose body `response.body` reads, and which says whether a site's service worker supplied it. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `response`.
events.name: page.response

events.description: The page opened a WebSocket, whose frames and close follow as `web_socket.frame_sent`, `web_socket.frame_received` and `web_socket.close`. Sent, with those, on each `page.on` call that listens to `web_socket`.
events.name: page.web_socket

events.description: A Run is being aborted: it stops at its next safe point. Lossless.
events.name: run.aborting

events.description: A Run's Lifecycle, Verdict or Completeness changed: it started running, or it ended. Lossless: while a subscriber's queue is full, the Run waits.
events.name: run.axes_changed

events.description: A Checkpoint of a Run is being written: on `run.checkpoint`, a pause, a migration, a clean stop or the periodic `checkpoint.interval`. Lossless.
events.name: run.checkpointing

events.description: A Run is being migrated to another machine: it checkpoints, then stops. Lossless.
events.name: run.migrating

events.description: A Run's progress changed, such as the program's own status line, a Human pause beginning or ending, or its end. Telemetry: a newer value of the same Run replaces an unsent one.
events.name: run.progress

events.description: A Run is stopping at its next safe point, with its cause: an abort, a pause or a migration. Lossless.
events.name: run.stopping

events.description: The sample crawl finished.
events.name: sample.crawled

events.description: A text was repeated.
events.name: sample.echoed

events.description: A page opened in the Session: one `session.new_page` or `run.new_page` opened, or a popup one of its pages opened. Published while `session.on` listens to `page`.
events.name: session.page

events.description: A page's WebSocket closed.
events.name: web_socket.close

events.description: A page's WebSocket received a message frame: its text, or a binary frame's bytes in Base64.
events.name: web_socket.frame_received

events.description: A page's WebSocket sent a message frame: its text, or a binary frame's bytes in Base64.
events.name: web_socket.frame_sent

Run the `daemon restart` the refusal's `fix` names, or upgrade the Client.

No partial file is left. Change the path.
exit_codes.name: path_not_writable

exit_codes.description: The bytes of a file could not be written: no space or quota left, or an I/O error, or any failure where the engine keeps its files. No partial file is left. Free space where the files go, or ask the Daemon's operator, then make the same call again.
exit_codes.name: file_write_failed

exit_codes.description: The engine ran out of memory or storage for the Run: it checkpointed and stopped it, or refused to start it where its run file would go. The details name the `resource`. Resume it once memory or space frees up, on an engine with a larger allowance, or with lower ceilings.
exit_codes.name: resources_exhausted

exit_codes.description: A Limit that covers the run has nothing left in its period; the details name its scope, its Usage kind, its period and when it starts again. Wait for the next period, or ask a person to raise it.
exit_codes.name: limit_reached

exit_codes.description: The Run ended `stopped`: a Limit, an abort, its timeout, a pause or the loss of its engine stopped it. Resume it by its Run ID.
exit_codes.name: run_stopped

exit_codes.description: `--require-verified` was given and the Run, or the Agent's Success check, ended with a Verdict other than `verified`: `rejected` or `needs_review`.
exit_codes.name: verdict_not_verified

exit_codes.description: `audit verify` found an entry that does not verify: the Audit log, or the export it was given, was edited, deleted from, reordered or truncated at the sequence its output names.
exit_codes.name: audit_log_not_intact

exit_codes.description: The command was interrupted (`SIGINT`, or `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` on Windows): its call was cancelled, and the Run it started checkpointed and stopped, resumable by its Run ID.
exit_codes.name: interrupted

exit_codes.description: The command was sent `SIGTERM`: its call was cancelled, and the Run it started checkpointed and stopped, resumable by its Run ID.
exit_codes.name: terminated

handler_requests.description: Asks the program's handler to process one attempt of a work item under its lease. Its answer carries the Records the attempt staged, committed once while the lease holds, or the handler's skip, which ends the request `skipped`; a failure, or no answer before the lease ends, commits nothing, and the work item is retried under the Run's policy, while a failure with the Error code `blocked` ends it `blocked` with the Block cause its details name. When the lease ends first, the engine sends `$/cancel` for the request; an answer that still comes is a late commit, refused with `lease_lost`.
handler_requests.name: crawl_request.handle

handler_requests.description: Asks a dialog handler to answer one dialog its page opened, named by its `dialog_id`, with `dialog.accept` or `dialog.dismiss`. The handler replies once it ends: a dialog it did not answer falls through to the handler before, and past the last one gets its default. A failure reply gives the dialog its default unless it was answered, removes the handler and raises `page_handler_failed`.
handler_requests.name: dialog.handle

handler_requests.description: Asks a route's handler to answer one request its URL pattern matched, named by its `route_id`, with `route.continue`, `route.fulfill`, `route.abort`, `route.fallback`, or `route.fetch` then `route.fulfill`. The handler replies once it ends: a request it did not answer falls back. A failure reply aborts the request unless it was answered, removes the route and raises `page_handler_failed`.
handler_requests.name: route.handle

operations.description: Exports the user's Audit log: every entry in sequence, each with the hash that chains it to the one before it, the anchor first when `audit.retention` pruned its beginning. The CLI's `audit export` writes them as JSONL, one entry per line, which `audit verify --file` verifies off the machine.
operations.name: audit.export

operations.description: Verifies the user's Audit log: every entry's hash chains it to the one before it, and the head file names the last one. Answers that it is intact, or the first sequence that does not verify, so an edited, deleted, reordered or truncated entry, a truncated tail included, shows.
operations.name: audit.verify

operations.description: Pins the changed key that stopped a host with `certificate_changed` in place of its pin, in the caller's partition, and records the accepted change in the Audit log; answers the new pin. Refused unless the key is the change the store holds for the host. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: certs.accept

operations.description: Removes the caller's pin of a host, and any change waiting for it, so its next connection under trust on first use pins again; nothing else removes a pin. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: certs.forget

operations.description: Lists the caller's pins in the known-certificates store: each host whose invalid certificate was accepted on first use, the SHA-256 of its public key, when and by which Run. Another person's pins on a shared Daemon are never listed. A row the engine cannot read is listed without its hash; it stops its host as a changed key.
operations.name: certs.list

operations.description: Shows each setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer that locked it, from the built-in defaults, the Operator policy, user configuration and the project configuration and run values given, and lists the keys only the other Product honours as that Product's.
operations.name: config.explain

operations.description: Reads the Operator policy of this engine's major: every entry of its `settings`, `lock` and `cap` tables, and its digest, which `config.policy_write` takes back. A person's entry: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: config.policy_read

operations.description: Writes changes to the Operator policy in one atomic write, only if its digest is still the one `config.policy_read` gave, every other byte of the file kept, and records the values before and after in the Audit log; a changed digest answers `policy_conflict` and writes nothing. A tightened cap reaches running Runs at their next admission point; every other change applies to new Runs. A person's entry: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: config.policy_write

operations.description: Writes user-level values to user configuration in one atomic write, every other byte of the file kept, once the resolver accepts them under the Operator policy, and records the values before and after in the Audit log; they apply to new Runs. A person's entry: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: config.user_write

operations.description: Sets the level of the engine's log events this Connection receives as `$/log` notifications, from the next one on: `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`, as `hello`'s `log_level` set it first. Each Connection has its own. Log events are telemetry: one the Connection is too slow to receive is dropped, and the next counts it in `dropped`.
operations.name: connection.set_log_level

operations.description: Replaces the Console key, which every major of the user shares, so every Console sign-in ends and everyone signs in again. A person's entry: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: console.rotate_key

operations.description: Offers this Connection's handler to a live crawl another Connection started, as each of `workers=N` handler processes does (ADR 0024): the engine leases the crawl's work items to it as `crawl_request.handle` requests too, as many at once as `crawl.handler.concurrency` allows on each Connection. Answers the crawl's Run report once the Run ends; cancelling the call stops new work items, while those already sent still expect their answers. A Run this engine does not run as a crawl fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: crawl.serve

operations.description: Starts a crawl from its seeds, and answers once its Run is started. The engine then leases each work item to the program's handler as a `crawl_request.handle` request, and the crawl's Run finishes once every work item is done, or, with `crawl.keep_alive`, once `run.finish` lets it and every work item is done. A Run ID works as `run.start`'s.
operations.name: crawl.start

operations.description: Adds one request to a crawl from inside a handler's attempt, a handler context's `enqueue`, and answers what the Frontier did with it: added, with its crawl request's ID and its URL as parsed, or not added, with its reason (`duplicate`, `out_of_scope`, `unsupported_scheme`, `invalid_url`, `max_depth`, `max_requests`, `path_budget` or a URL cap's name). A relative URL resolves against the document's base URL: its `<base href>`, resolved against the URL the document was reached at after its redirects, or that URL itself. A request is `duplicate` when one of its identity was already admitted: its method, its URL's key (the fragment, `utm_*`, `gclid`, `fbclid`, empty pairs and `;jsessionid=` dropped, the parameters sorted) and its body's hash, or the `key` the program declares in their place; it is still fetched at its own URL. The request sits one level deeper than the one whose attempt added it. An attempt whose lease no longer holds fails with `attempt_ended`.
operations.name: crawl_request.enqueue

operations.description: Adds every link a locator matches on the page a handler's attempt was given, a handler context's `enqueueLinks`, each a `GET` of its `href` resolved against the document's base URL (its `<base href>`, resolved against the URL the document was reached at after its redirects, or that URL itself), its query percent-encoded in the document's encoding as a browser encodes it, and answers each matched element in document order: added, with its crawl request's ID and URL; not added, with its reason, as `crawl_request.enqueue` answers; `no_link` for an element without an `href`; or `skipped_by_payload` for one whose entry in `payloads` is `null`. Every link takes `payload`, or its own entry of `payloads`, the program's Payload function's answers for the elements `crawl_request.links` read; a Payload that does not fit its Label fails the call with `payload_invalid` and adds none. `limit` adds at most that many links: once they are added, each later element whose link the Frontier would judge is not added, with `link_limit`. `include` and `exclude` only narrow the crawl's scope; a pattern the engine cannot match fails with `pattern_unsupported`. A page no fetch tier serves fails with `closed`, and an attempt whose lease no longer holds with `attempt_ended`.
operations.name: crawl_request.enqueue_links

operations.description: Reads each element a locator matches on the page a handler's attempt was given, in document order, as a handler context's `enqueueLinks` gives them to its Payload function: its `href` as written, its URL (the `href` resolved against the document's base URL, its query percent-encoded in the document's encoding, as a browser encodes it), its text and its attributes. A page no fetch tier serves fails with `closed`, a selector that is no CSS selector with `invalid_params`, and an attempt whose lease no longer holds with `attempt_ended`.
operations.name: crawl_request.links

operations.description: Pushes one Record into a Dataset the crawl declares from inside a handler's attempt, a handler context's `push`, and answers once it is staged: it commits once with the attempt's other outputs when the handler returns, and is discarded with them when the attempt ends any other way. The Record is checked first: a Dataset the crawl does not declare fails with `dataset_unknown`; a Record that is no JSON object, fails its Dataset's JSON Schema or lacks one of its key's fields fails with `record_invalid`, naming each issue's path, and is not staged: its rejection is staged instead, entering the Dataset's rejection table (`run.rejected_records`) if the attempt commits, while the attempt keeps what it staged before. An attempt that already ended fails with `attempt_ended`.
operations.name: crawl_request.push

operations.description: Says whether the Daemon is live and ready to take a new Run, and why not: what its ops listener's `/livez` and `/readyz` answer with a status alone.
operations.name: daemon.health

operations.description: Says what the Daemon runs as, where it listens, how many Clients and live Runs it has, when it stops idle, and its live heap.
operations.name: daemon.status

operations.description: Stops the Daemon once it answered: its live Runs stop, each resumable from its own state, and its runtime file and socket are removed.
operations.name: daemon.stop

operations.description: Lists the Datasets a crawl's Run declares, in the order declared, each with its JSON Schema, its key and how many Records the crawl committed into it, a Hook dropped and were rejected into its rejection table, read from the Run's committed state. A Run no crawl wrote declares none.
operations.name: dataset.list

operations.description: Reads one page of a Dataset's committed Records, paged by key: the Records that meet `filter` (conditions on top-level fields, and the `wall` marker a Record's Provenance carries or not), in the order of `sort` (one top-level field, Records that lack it last, then by number), each value keeping only the fields `columns` names, at most `limit`. Filtering, sorting and column selection run in the engine. A page starts after the Record `after` names, the previous page's `next`, and reads only the Records committed through `through`, the number the first page answered, so Records committed meanwhile never make a page repeat or skip one. A Dataset the crawl does not declare fails with `dataset_unknown`; a field name holding `"`, or a `limit` outside 1 to 1000, with `invalid_params`.
operations.name: dataset.page

operations.description: Runs one read-only SQL statement, `SELECT` or `WITH`, over the runs `runs` selects, at most 100, and answers its columns, its first rows up to `limit` (at most `dataset.query.max_rows`) and how many rows it produced. Each run's tables are table functions that take its Run ID: `records(run)` (each Dataset's committed Records), `rejected_records(run)` and `datasets(run)`, which read its run file read-only; secret fields are never columns. Any other statement, a write, `ATTACH`, `INSTALL`, `LOAD`, `COPY`, a read of a file or URL, or a run not selected fails with `query_invalid`; past `timeout.dataset_query` it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, and past `dataset.query.memory_limit` with `query_memory_exceeded`. A run that does not exist fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: dataset.query

operations.description: Answers a dialog by accepting it, a prompt with `prompt_text`, or else its default value; it answers once the page closed the dialog.
operations.name: dialog.accept

operations.description: Answers a dialog by dismissing it, as its Cancel button does; it answers once the page closed the dialog.
operations.name: dialog.dismiss

operations.description: Saves a Download's file, which the engine keeps with its Run, whole or not at all. An Attached engine given the program's path writes it through a hidden temporary file beside it, synced and renamed over it, creating missing folders and replacing a file there; any other engine writes nothing on its own machine and sends the file in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, for the SDK to write. Answers the file's size and SHA-256. A path that cannot be written raises `path_not_writable`, and full or failing storage `file_write_failed`, leaving the path as it was.
operations.name: download.save_as

operations.description: Says which Product the engine runs as, its Product version and major, and the protocol version it speaks.
operations.name: engine.info

operations.description: Subscribes to the engine's events. The call stays in flight, sending its events in `$/events` batches, never more than the credits granted with `$/credit`, until it is cancelled. No producer waits for a subscription: a lossless event is never dropped unseen, and a subscription whose queue is full falls behind, dropping its queued lossless events, and next sends `events.resync`, then the stream. A telemetry event is coalesced with the unsent one of the same kind and scope, and counts it as `dropped`. Given `after`, the last event read, it resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as after a Daemon restart. Given `system_info`, it also takes the Resource governor's periodic `engine.system_info`.
operations.name: events.subscribe

operations.description: Saves an Export's file, which the engine keeps in its Run's folder, whole or not at all. An Attached engine given the program's path writes it through a hidden temporary file beside it, synced and renamed over it, creating missing folders and replacing a file there; any other engine writes nothing on its own machine and sends the file in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, for the SDK to write. Answers the file's size and SHA-256. A path that cannot be written raises `path_not_writable`, and full or failing storage `file_write_failed`, leaving the path as it was.
operations.name: export.save_as

operations.description: Sends an Export's bytes, which the engine keeps in its Run's folder, in order, in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, and answers its size and SHA-256 once every byte is sent. Nothing is written on either machine: a program that writes the bytes itself meets its own language's file errors.
operations.name: export.stream

operations.description: Removes a key from a live Run's Key-value store and answers whether it existed. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), the removal is staged with the attempt, and whether the key existed counts what the attempt staged.
operations.name: key_value_store.delete

operations.description: Answers the JSON value a Run's Key-value store holds for a key, as committed, or null when the key is absent. A key holding bytes fails with `value_invalid`, naming `getBytes`. Takes no writer lock, so it reads a Run no program holds without resuming it. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), it reads what the attempt staged first.
operations.name: key_value_store.get

operations.description: Answers the bytes and content type a Run's Key-value store holds for a key, as committed, or null when the key is absent. A key holding JSON fails with `value_invalid`, naming `get`. Takes no writer lock. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), it reads what the attempt staged first.
operations.name: key_value_store.get_bytes

operations.description: Sends the committed keys of a Run's Key-value store that start with `prefix`, in the order of their Unicode scalar values, in `$/key` notifications, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers how many it sent. Takes no writer lock.
operations.name: key_value_store.keys

operations.description: Commits a JSON value for a key in a live Run's Key-value store, replacing the one it held: the last commit wins. A null value fails with `value_invalid`; remove a key with `delete`. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), the write is staged with the attempt and commits or is discarded with it; once the attempt ended, it fails with `attempt_ended`.
operations.name: key_value_store.set

operations.description: Commits bytes with their content type for a key in a live Run's Key-value store, replacing what it held: the last commit wins. Bytes over 1 MiB are kept as a file in the Run's folder, which its Checkpoints carry.
operations.name: key_value_store.set_bytes

operations.description: Clicks the element the locator matches once it is unique, visible, enabled, stable and receiving the click (the guard, ADR 0019); a click that lands on another element is cancelled and sent again, until `timeout.action` passes. A click that starts a navigation of the page answers once that navigation's document committed or it ended without one, within `timeout.navigation` (ADR 0085).
operations.name: locator.click

operations.description: Runs a page function, as `page.evaluate` does, with the array of every element the locator matches first, none included, and its one JSON argument second, and answers its result, awaited, as JSON; the elements stay in the page, so a result holding one raises `page_value_invalid`. A selector the page does not parse raises `invalid_params`, and an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance.
operations.name: locator.evaluate_all

operations.description: Replaces the text of the field the locator matches, once it is unique, visible, enabled and editable, with text the page receives as typed input, until `timeout.action` passes. An input whose value a person picks rather than types (a date, a time, a month, a week, a local date and time, a colour or a range) has its value set, firing `input` and `change`, and a value it does not take fails with `invalid_params`.
operations.name: locator.fill

operations.description: Focuses the element the locator matches, once it is unique, visible and enabled, and presses a key or a combination on it as a keyboard does, until `timeout.action` passes. A press that starts a navigation of the page answers once that navigation's document committed or it ended without one, within `timeout.navigation` (ADR 0085).
operations.name: locator.press

operations.description: Waits until the element the locator matches is in the state: attached or visible, one element; detached, none; hidden, none or one not visible. The locator is resolved again at each check, so a re-render that replaces its element changes nothing. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, several matches raise `target_not_unique` listing them, and anything else `deadline_exceeded` naming the state.
operations.name: locator.wait_for

operations.description: Waits until the number of elements the locator matches is within the count, and answers it. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: locator.wait_for_count

operations.description: Waits, checking from when the call arrives, until a page function called with the one element the locator matches first and its one JSON argument second answers a truthy result, and answers that result as JSON, as `page.wait_for_function` does. The locator is resolved again at each check, so a re-render that replaces its element changes nothing, and a check while none or several elements match counts as falsy. A value outside JSON raises `page_value_invalid`, an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`, and a selector the page does not parse `invalid_params`. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: locator.wait_for_function

operations.description: Adds a domain whose consent wall a Run met, or `*` for every domain, to `consent.domains` in user configuration, so the next runs accept its consent walls instead of raising `blocked` with `consent_required`, and records the answer in the Audit log with the warning of what the person takes on; answers whether it added it. One call, no confirmation asked. A domain that file lists already adds nothing; an Operator policy that locks `consent.domains` refuses it with `setting_locked`. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt. The `consent_wall` items it covers leave the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.allow_consent_domain

operations.description: Adds a registrable domain, with its required reason, to `wall.denied_domains` in the Operator policy, creating the file when there is none, so no run reads past its Walls or refetches its pages whatever another layer allows (ADR 0052), and records the denial and its reason in the Audit log; answers whether it added it. One call, no confirmation asked. A managed Operator policy refuses it with `setting_locked`. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt. The `wall_refetch_stopped` item of the domain leaves the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.deny_wall_domain

operations.description: Hides an item of "Needs you" whose source lets a person dismiss it, for every Client, and answers whether it did; an item the list no longer holds, or one only resolving it removes, stays as it is. The item leaves the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.dismiss

operations.description: Lists what waits for a person across every Run in the Run index and the stores beside it, the longest waiting first, a page at a time: `after` takes the `next` of the page before. `kinds` keeps the items of those kinds. Each change after the answer arrives as `needs_you.changed` on the event stream.
operations.name: needs_you.list

operations.description: Removes a domain on which a Run's refetch stopped from the layer of `wall.refetch_domains` that lists it, user configuration or else the Operator policy, every other entry and byte of the file kept, and records the answer in the Audit log; answers whether it removed it. When only `*` covers the domain there, `instead_of_star` gives the registrable domains that replace `*`, and without it the call is refused with `invalid_params`. A domain only project configuration lists is changed in that file, never here. A managed Operator policy, or one that locks the key against user configuration, refuses it with `setting_locked`. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt. The `wall_refetch_stopped` item leaves the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.remove_refetch_domain

operations.description: Registers a script, registered when the call arrives, that runs in the main world of every document the page loads afterwards, its frames' included, before the document's own scripts: the call stays in flight, and a navigation sent after it waits until the script is registered. A function is called with its one JSON argument. The Session's Provenance marks the main-world injection. Cancelling the call, as closing its `Subscription` does, removes the script; it answers when the page closes.
operations.name: page.add_init_script

operations.description: Reads a page body by its handle, for a Client that cannot read the handle's file: sends the body in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers its size.
operations.name: page.body

operations.description: Closes the page, a popup as any other: its calls in flight raise `call_cancelled` naming the program, it emits `close`, and a later call on it raises `closed`, while closing it again changes nothing. Its `beforeunload` handlers do not run unless `run_before_unload` is set: the page then closes once they let it, a dialog they raise going to its dialog handlers, and the call answers without waiting for that.
operations.name: page.close

operations.description: Runs a page function in the page's main frame with its one JSON argument, in the main world, where the page's globals are, or in an isolated world the page neither sees nor hooks, and answers its result, awaited, as JSON; a result of `undefined` answers no value. A value outside JSON in the result raises `page_value_invalid` naming its path and kind, and an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`. It is no gesture: it runs beside the page's actions. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance.
operations.name: page.evaluate

operations.description: Reads the formats a request names from the page's current document, each read from one serialization of it, and answers only those, with the document's URL, its base URL and, when a format it names is read from the main content (`markdown` of the main content or fit, `html` of the main content, `text`), whether the document has main content. A document with no main content answers those formats empty and `main_content: "none"`, a value. It needs neither layout nor pixels, so every tier serves it.
operations.name: page.formats

operations.description: Goes back one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go back to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_back

operations.description: Goes forward one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go forward to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_forward

operations.description: Navigates the page to a URL and waits for its document's `load` event, or the state `wait_until` names, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A file the browser downloads, such as a PDF, answers no response and emits `page.download`. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`, a redirect loop `too_many_redirects`, a document whose body broke off `response_truncated`, unless the navigation answered at `commit`, and one past its `timeout`, or `timeout.navigation` without one, `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.goto

operations.description: Listens to one of the page's events, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and the engine sends that event of the page on the call itself, in `$/events` batches naming it, never more than the credits granted it with `$/credit`, its positions counting the call's own events from 1. Only the Connection that armed it gets them, never the engine's shared event stream. Lossless: past 1,024 events unsent, as when its Client grants too few credits, the call raises `page_events_lost` once it sent those. Cancelling the call, as closing its `Subscription` does, removes the listener; it answers when the page closes or its Run ends, once it sent the events it holds. The page's console and uncaught exceptions, its out-of-process frames' included, are read only while a call listens to `console` or `page_error`.
operations.name: page.on

operations.description: Hands the page's JavaScript dialogs to the program, armed when the call arrives: Playwright's `page.on('dialog')`. The call stays in flight, and for each dialog the engine sends `dialog.handle`, which the handler answers with `dialog.accept` or `dialog.dismiss`. Later handlers come first and the first answer wins; a handler that ends without one falls through, and past the last one, or with none, an `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt` is dismissed and a `beforeunload` dialog accepted, so a handler that answers nothing never stalls the page. Cancelling the call removes the handler; a handler that fails ends it with `page_handler_failed`, the dialog getting its default.
operations.name: page.on_dialog

operations.description: Loads the page's document again and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, and one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`.
operations.name: page.reload

operations.description: Sends a request from inside the page's Session's browser, with its cookies, through the browser-fetch tier and the page's interception (its domain policy, never its routes), from a context no service worker controls, and answers the response whatever its status, a 429 included; `response.body` reads its kept body, and raises `response_truncated` for one that broke off. A count of redirects above 19 is refused with `setting_invalid`, a chain past its count raises `too_many_redirects`, and a body whose content coding fails to decode `navigation_failed`.
operations.name: page.request

operations.description: Routes the page's requests whose URL matches to the program, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and for each such request the engine sends `route.handle`, which the handler answers with `route.continue`, `route.fulfill`, `route.abort`, `route.fallback`, or `route.fetch` then `route.fulfill`. Page routes come before Session routes, later routes first, and the first answer wins; a handler that ends without one falls back, and past the last route the request goes on to the network, so an unanswered route never stalls a request. What a route sends on still passes the domain policy. Cancelling the call removes the route; a handler that fails ends it with `page_handler_failed`.
operations.name: page.route

operations.description: Runs a page function in the page's main frame, as `page.evaluate` does, again at each polling interval and in each new document, until its result is truthy, and answers that result as JSON. A value outside JSON raises `page_value_invalid`, an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_function

operations.description: Waits until the page's document reached the load state: at once when it already did. `networkidle` is reached once the document fired `load` and no request of the page was in flight for 500 ms since, WebSocket and server-sent-event connections and a service worker's own requests left out. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_load_state

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until the page sends a request whose URL matches, and answers it, so a request an action triggers is caught by a waiter sent before the action. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_request

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until a request of the page whose URL matches has finished, a hop that a redirect ended included, and answers it with its response, whose body the engine reads and keeps, so `response.body` never fails for it but for a redirect's, which has none. A request that fails is not waited for. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_request_finished

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until a request of the page whose URL matches gets its response, a redirect's included, and answers both, so a response an action triggers is caught by a waiter sent before the action, even one that arrives before the program awaits it. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_response

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until the page's URL matches: at once when it already does, else on a committed navigation, then until its document reaches `wait_until`, or on a change within the document, a `pushState`, a `replaceState` or a hash change. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_url
