operations.description: Reads the body of the response a page's request got, once the request finished, as a page body's handle: kept already for a response `page.wait_for_request_finished` answered, and otherwise read from the browser, on the session of the frame that loaded it. A body the browser no longer holds, or a redirect's, which has none, raises `body_unavailable`, whose fix names `page.wait_for_request_finished`; one that broke off raises `response_truncated`, never returned as whole. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, a request that has not ended fails it with `deadline_exceeded`; a page that ends under it raises what ended it, as a call on the page does.
operations.name: response.body

operations.description: Answers a route's request by failing it with a network error its page sees, `failed` unless named; nothing reaches the network.
operations.name: route.abort

operations.description: Answers a route's request by sending it on, with any overrides, past every other route: the domain policy judges what it sends.
operations.name: route.continue

operations.description: Answers a route's request by passing it, with any overrides, to the route registered before, from the page's first route to the Session's last; past the last route it goes on to the network.
operations.name: route.fallback

operations.description: Sends a route's request on, with any overrides, past every other route, as `route.continue` does, and answers the response it got, its body kept; the handler then answers the request with `route.fulfill`, or, ending without one, the page gets that response.
operations.name: route.fetch

operations.description: Answers a route's request with a response of the program's own, or the one `route.fetch` returned with its changes; nothing reaches the network.
operations.name: route.fulfill

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point, `stopped` and `incomplete`: no attempt in flight commits, and its work items return to pending. Answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. A Run whose engine died is stopped by this engine, which takes its writer role at the next run epoch; a Run another engine writes is stopped by that engine, the owner the Run index names.
operations.name: run.abort

operations.description: Adds one seed to a running crawl, `run.addSeed`, committed at once, and answers as an enqueue does: added, with its crawl request's ID and its URL as parsed, or not added, with its reason (`duplicate`, `unsupported_scheme`, `invalid_url` or a cap's name). A relative seed is `invalid_url`. An idle `crawl.keep_alive` crawl takes it and goes on. Through a handler's context, naming its `attempt`, it is bound to that attempt: once the attempt ended it fails with `attempt_ended`. A Run this engine does not run as a live crawl, or a crawl already ending its Run, fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.add_seed

operations.description: Takes a stream of seeds for a running crawl, `run.addSeeds`, and answers each as `run.add_seed` does, in order, so a million seeds never sit in memory. The engine grants the call 256 credits with `$/credit`, one seed each; the Client sends seeds in `$/seeds {id, seeds, end?}` batches, never more than its credits, and the engine commits each batch, sends its answers in one `$/enqueued {id, answers}` and grants as many credits again. Once it answered the batch marked `end`, the call answers how many seeds were added and how many were not. Cancelling it keeps the seeds already answered. A batch beyond the credits granted, or a seed that is no seed, fails the call with `invalid_params`; a Run this engine does not run as a live crawl, or a crawl already ending its Run, fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.add_seeds

operations.description: Writes a Checkpoint of a live Run now, through SQLite's online backup, where `location` says or where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, and answers it once its file is complete, with its size, digest, run epoch and journal position. A Checkpoint the engine cannot write fails with `file_write_failed` and leaves no file.
operations.name: run.checkpoint

operations.description: Discards a Run that ended or was interrupted, for good, so that nothing of it is left behind (ADRs 0001, 0002, 0015 and 0036): its wrapped data key is overwritten and its run folder removed, with its run file, page bodies, browser profiles and the Checkpoints written there; in the per-install layout its rows are deleted from the install database with `secure_delete` on, then `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, so neither the database nor its `-wal` and `-shm` files hold its bytes. Its Run index row stays, marked `erased`, without its tags or status line. A Profile directory it used in place and a Borrowed browser are the person's own and are never touched (ADR 0056), nor are Checkpoints written elsewhere. A later `run.start` under its Run ID starts a new Run; discarding a Run already discarded changes nothing. A Run this engine runs fails with `run_live`, one whose writer lock another engine holds with `run_in_use`, and a Run ID no Run has with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.discard

operations.description: Writes an Export of one Dataset of a crawl's Run: the Records it committed when the call is made, in number order, in the format named: `json`, one array of the Records' values, indented as `export.json.indent` says; `jsonl`, one value per line; `csv`, `xlsx`, `html_table` and `markdown`, a table of one column per field seen in any of its Records, in first-seen order, and one row per Record; `parquet`, `avro` and `arrow_ipc`, the same columns typed: a column whose values are all `true` or `false` is boolean, all whole numbers a 64-bit integer, all numbers a 64-bit float, and any other a string holding each cell's text, every column nullable, an Avro field's name made a valid Avro name with the field's own in its `doc`; `xml`, a root element named by `export.xml.root` holding one element per Record named by `export.xml.record`, each field an element of its name (`field` with a `name` attribute where its name is no XML name), an object's fields as elements, an array's values as `item` elements, and `null` an empty element with `xsi:nil="true"`; `rss` and `atom`, a feed named after the Dataset of one item or entry per Record, its title, link, date and summary taken from the fields the `export.feed.*` settings name. Every text Export is UTF-8 with no BOM unless `export.csv.bom` puts one on CSV, characters written as themselves (a character XML 1.0 cannot hold as U+FFFD in XML and feeds) and each value as it was committed: a table cell holds a string as its text, a number, `true` or `false` as JSON writes it, nothing for `null` or a field its Record lacks, and an object or array as its JSON text, or, in CSV under `export.csv.nested: flatten`, an object's fields in dotted columns. A Record whose page was read past a Wall carries its Wall marker, `{kind, vendor?}` as its Provenance holds it, as a `#wall` field in every format but the feeds, where it is a category of the scheme `urn:goodfetch:wall` naming its kind; `wall` set to `true` writes only those Records, `false` only the others. `compression` `gzip` or `zstd` compresses the whole file. Its `settings` and `project` are the run layer and the project configuration its `export.*` settings resolve under; a value the format cannot take fails with `setting_invalid`. Answers the Export, with its Record count, its last Record's number, its size and its SHA-256, only once its file is whole in the Run's folder, where `export.save_as` and `export.stream` read it. Records committed after the call starts are not in it. A write the engine's storage refuses fails with `file_write_failed`, side `engine`, leaving no unfinished file, as does a call while that storage is at the `critical` level, before any byte is written. A Dataset the crawl does not declare fails with `dataset_unknown`.
operations.name: run.export

operations.description: Reads from a crawl's committed state the requests whose latest outcome is `failed`, and with `blocked` also `blocked`, each with that outcome: exactly those `run.retry_failed` re-admits with the same option. A skip is a decision and is never listed.
operations.name: run.failed_requests

operations.description: Lets a Run finish and answers its Run report: a Run its program drives ends at once, `finished` and `complete`; a crawl ends once its work items are done, and a keep-alive crawl (`crawl.keep_alive`), which waits for new work while nothing is left, ends once this call lets it and its work items are done. A Run something stopped first answers its report saying `stopped`. A Run that ended `failed` fails the call with the error that failed it, and a write at its end that failed, such as its Plan file's, with that write's error. Cancelling the call, or its `timeout` passing, which fails it with `deadline_exceeded`, ends only the wait.
operations.name: run.finish

operations.description: Lists the Runs of the Run index of the user and major, of either Product (ADRs 0031 and 0098): each row with its tags, Lifecycle, Verdict, Completeness, start and end, the engine that owns it while it is live, and its presence, a Run whose state is gone `missing` and one discarded on purpose `erased`, never left out. The engine filters by tags, the Recipe, Schedule, occurrence and trigger its reserved `goodfetch.` tags name, Product, each axis, start and end time, and a text found in its Run ID or tags, and sorts by the key given; Watch runs are left out unless `watch_runs` asks for them (ADR 0036).
operations.name: run.list

operations.description: Migrates a live Run: checkpoints it where `location` says or where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `migrate`, to be resumed from that Checkpoint on another machine. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.migrate

operations.description: Opens a page in the Run's default Session, which the first call opens with the Run's settings and every later call shares; `page.session()` reaches it. The first page launches the Run's browser, so a missing browser build raises its code from this call.
operations.name: run.new_page

operations.description: Opens a Session of the Run's own: its own browser context, with its own cookies, storage, identity and proxy, sharing the Run's browser process, so two Sessions of a Run never share a login. It opens from `source`, or else from the Run's `session.source`, or fresh; `session.source` in its own `settings` is refused with `setting_not_applicable`. The Run's first Session launches its browser, so a missing browser build raises its code from this call.
operations.name: run.new_session

operations.description: Reads a crawl's outcomes from its committed state, in commit order: from the first, after a position, or with `after: "now"` from the next commit. Its filters, `kinds`, `labels` and `codes` (an Error code any of the request's failed attempts failed with), run in the engine. While the Run is live and nothing new matches, it waits for the next commit; a page says `ended` once the Run has ended, or has no live writer, and nothing more matches. A reader never slows the Run. A request `run.retry_failed` re-admits ends again, and its later outcome supersedes the earlier one by `request.id`.
operations.name: run.outcomes

operations.description: Pauses a live Run: checkpoints it, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `pause` and resumable by its Run ID with `run.resume`, after a restart too. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.pause

operations.description: Reads a Run's progress: what it does and why it waits. Without `after`, it answers at once; given `after`, the position of the value the reader last read, it waits for a change and answers the latest value, so values in between are coalesced. The value whose `last` is true ends the sequence: the Run ended, and its `lifecycle` and `stop_reason` say how, or no engine works it (`writer: none`) until a start with its Run ID resumes it. A Run another engine works is read through that engine, the owner the Run index names, and one no engine works from its committed state; a read never takes the Run's writer lock. A Run ID the Run index does not list fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.progress

operations.description: Reads the committed Records of one Dataset of a crawl's Run in number order, from the first, or after the number `after`, which resumes a reader from the last Record it handled. Each Record goes in a `$/record` notification with its number, its value, its request's ID and URL and when it was committed, one per credit granted with `$/credit`. While the Run is live it follows the Run, sending each Record once it commits; once the Run has ended, or has no live writer, and every Record is sent, it answers how many it sent and the last one's number. With `through`, such as the number `dataset.page` answers as the last committed, it reads no Record numbered past it and answers once it sent every Record through it, a live Run's included. Records are read from the Run's committed state on a connection of their own, so a reader that grants no credit never slows the crawl. With `wall` set to `true` it reads only the Records whose page was read past a Wall, which their Provenance marks, and with `false` only the others (ADR 0052). A Dataset the crawl does not declare fails with `dataset_unknown`.
operations.name: run.records

operations.description: Reads one Dataset's rejection table from a crawl's committed state: each Record rejected rather than committed, numbered from 1 in commit order, with the Record as JSON, the reason, each issue's path, the Hook when one rejected it, and the request's ID and URL. It starts at the first entry, or after `after`, the number a reader last handled. While the Run is live and nothing follows, it waits for the next commit; a page says `ended` once the Run has ended, or has no live writer, and no entry follows. A reader never slows the Run. A Dataset the crawl does not declare fails with `dataset_unknown`.
operations.name: run.rejected_records

operations.description: Reads a Run's report: at once for a Run that ended, and at its end for a live one, which the read never ends. A Run another engine works is read through that engine, and one no engine works from its committed state, never taking its writer lock. A Run that has no live writer and has not ended fails with `run_interrupted`, whose `fix` names a start with its Run ID, and a Run ID the Run index does not list with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.report

operations.description: Resumes an interrupted Run from its committed state, its run file on this machine or the Checkpoint `checkpoint` names: it takes the Run's writer lock and the next run epoch, so every write of an earlier writer is refused, and redoes the work since that state; its recorded Clean-up rules digest is kept. A live Run is answered as it is, `existing`; a finished one as it is. A Run bound to another machine fails with `session_bound_to_machine`, and a Checkpoint of a format version this engine cannot read with `format_version_unsupported`.
operations.name: run.resume

operations.description: Re-admits, in the same Run and its Datasets, every request of a crawl whose latest outcome is `failed`, and with `blocked` also `blocked`: exactly those `run.failed_requests` lists with the same option. Each keeps its ID, Label, Payload and depth; its attempts count on, with a fresh `crawl.retry.max`. A skip is a decision and is never re-admitted. It answers how many it re-admitted, 0 when there was nothing to retry. On a crawl this engine runs, the requests join its work at once, unless the crawl is already ending its Run: the call then waits for that end and re-admits them as on an ended Run. On an ended Run with requests to retry, the Run returns to `running` under `settings`, as a resume does, its Verdict and Completeness given anew when it ends, and the calling Connection serves its handlers. A Run with no writer that has not ended fails with `run_interrupted`: resume it first. It is not sent again after a lost Connection, which fails it with `connection_lost`: `run.failed_requests` then lists the requests still to retry.
operations.name: run.retry_failed

operations.description: Lists each seed's answer, in the order the crawl's start gave them, as the Frontier answered it when the Run began: added, with its crawl request's ID and its URL as parsed, or not added, with its reason (`duplicate`, `domain_policy`, `unsupported_scheme`, `invalid_url` or a cap's name). A relative seed is `invalid_url`, since nothing gives it a base. So a crawl that does nothing says why. Read from the Run's committed state, so it works on a Run no program holds.
operations.name: run.seeds

operations.description: Sets the program's own status line about a live Run, at most 512 characters, which replaces the one before: kept in the Run's state, so a resume keeps it, shown in its Run index row and carried on its progress, `run.progress`. Answers the Run's progress. A Run this engine does not run fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.set_progress_message

operations.description: Starts a Run its program drives, and answers once it is started. A Run ID names the Run for good: a start with an existing Run ID returns that Run as it is when the caller and the inputs match, and fails with `run_conflict` otherwise.
operations.name: run.start

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point with a Checkpoint, `stopped` and `incomplete` as an abort by its program, resumable by its Run ID, and answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. The wait is bounded by `timeout.close`, or the call's `timeout`: past it, the call fails with `deadline_exceeded` and the Run still stops at its next safe point. A Run that ended `failed` fails the call as `run.finish` does.
operations.name: run.stop

operations.description: Answers what a Run used, as the Usage ledger charged it: its model calls and tokens, browser time, proxy bytes, requests, paid solves and Paid fetches, each Limit that applies to it with what is left of it, and whether it is uncapped. An ended Run answers its report's Usage.
operations.name: run.usage

operations.description: Visits sample pages, each repeating a text.
operations.name: sample.crawl

deprecated.note: A sample entry, which the real catalog replaces.

operations.description: Repeats a text back to the caller.
operations.name: sample.echo

operations.description: Closes the Session: its pages and its browser context close, and its pages' admissions go back to the Resource governor; a Borrowed browser is never closed. A later call on the Session or one of its pages raises `closed`, and closing it again changes nothing.
operations.name: session.close

operations.description: Opens a page in the Session, with its cookies and storage, and its own settings. Once the Session is closed, it raises `closed`.
operations.name: session.new_page

operations.description: Listens to one of the Session's events, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and the engine publishes that event of the Session on its event stream, lossless, which `events.subscribe` reads under its credits. Cancelling the call removes the listener; it answers when the Session closes or its Run ends.
operations.name: session.on

operations.description: Lists the Session's open pages, in the order they opened: those the program opened and the popups its pages opened. Once the Session is closed, it raises `closed`.
operations.name: session.pages

operations.description: Routes the requests of every page of the Session whose URL matches to the program, as `page.route` does, after the page's own routes.
operations.name: session.route

operations.description: Lists the Console's sign-ins that have not ended, each with its person, when it was created and when it was last used, never its cookie. A person's entry: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: sign_in.list

operations.description: Ends one Console sign-in, so its cookie signs nobody in, such as a lost laptop's. A person's entry: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: sign_in.revoke

operations.description: Lists every Limit of the Usage ledger, by scope, with the Usage charged and held against it in its current period and what is left.
operations.name: usage.list

operations.description: Sets a Limit to a person's amount, in place of every Limit of its scope, Usage kind, currency and period but a managed Operator policy's, keeping the Usage counted. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: usage.raise

operations.description: Adds a Limit of the caller's own to the Usage ledger, which holds beside the others: the tightest one holds, so it can only lower what applies. Answers it with its Usage.
operations.name: usage.set

plugin_kinds.description: Chooses the pages the sample crawl visits.

methods.description: Says whether the sample crawl visits a page.
methods.name: admit

plugin_kinds.name: sample_page_filter

plugin_kinds.description: Keeps values by key for the sample operations.

methods.description: Keeps a value under a key.
methods.name: put

plugin_kinds.name: sample_store

settings.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.
settings.name: admission.max_requests_per_minute

settings.description: Whether an engine process also sends each new Audit log entry, the hash with it, as an OpenTelemetry event to the OTLP/HTTP collector `otlp.logs_endpoint` names: off by default, and nothing is sent while `otlp.logs_endpoint` is unset. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: audit.otlp

settings.description: How long the user's Audit log keeps an entry, in milliseconds, such as 15552000000 for the six months the EU AI Act asks of high-risk deployers. Unset, the default, nothing is ever pruned. Set, each append first prunes the entries older than it from the log's beginning only, leaving an anchor entry that carries the last pruned hash, from which `audit verify` checks the rest, and a pruning record at the tail. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: audit.retention

settings.description: The resource kinds the Session's pages never load, failed as `BlockedByClient` by its interception before every navigation: any of `image`, `media`, `font` and `stylesheet`; none by default. The never-block list still loads a challenge's own. In `standard` and `stealth` the Run warns once per Session that the site can see the missing loads.
settings.name: browser.block_resources

settings.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent.
settings.name: browser.headless

settings.description: Whether a site's service workers run in the Session's pages: `allow` (the default on Chromium) runs them under the Session's interception, each worker's own requests passing the domain policy, the Filter lists and the Session's routes, never a page's routes; `block` makes `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` reject as on a failed fetch of the worker's script, `register` staying the browser's own function, so that every request of a page reaches its routes.
settings.name: browser.service_workers

settings.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: browser_cache.max_unused_age

settings.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.
settings.name: checkpoint.interval

settings.description: The OCI repository the daily channel is pulled from, `host[:port]/path`: Goodfetch's own on ghcr.io by default, or a mirror of it, which `clean_up.update = daily` makes the configured destination. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.
settings.name: clean_up.channel

settings.description: How long fetching a version of the Clean-up rules from its sources may take at a Run's start or resume: past it, a Run holds to the newest version this machine has, and a `clean_up.version` it cannot fetch refuses the start. 30 s.
settings.name: clean_up.fetch_timeout

settings.description: The URL `clean_up.update = upstream` fetches each Filter list from, by list: `ads` (EasyList), `trackers` (EasyPrivacy), `annoyances` (Fanboy Annoyance) and `unbreak` (Brave's unbreak list); their authors' own URLs by default, or a mirror's. Each must be `https`. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.
settings.name: clean_up.lists

settings.description: Where a new Run's Clean-up rules come from: `release` (the default), the set this release pins, with the embedded part as fallback; `daily`, the opt-in daily channel, whose registry it makes a configured destination, refused with `capability_unavailable` until the engine checks the channel's signature; `upstream`, the Filter lists from their authors' URLs, which it makes configured destinations. A Run holds to the version it starts with for its whole life, a resume included; `egress.offline` turns the fetching off. Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: clean_up.update

settings.description: The exact version of the Clean-up rules a new Run holds to, by its digest `sha256:<hex>` as Provenance names it, instead of the newest one `clean_up.update` gives: a daily version it names is fetched from the daily channel, and it is exempt from the channel's expiry and its refusal of older versions. None by default.
settings.name: clean_up.version

settings.description: The registrable domains on which a run accepts a consent wall, a Consent prompt with no refusal that covers the content or offers payment instead, rather than raising `blocked` with `consent_required`; `*` only when written. A prompt that offers a refusal is still refused there. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer.
settings.name: consent.domains

settings.description: Whether a browser Session answers Consent prompts: on by default in every Access mode, refusing each prompt in every frame and hiding one with no refusal that leaves the content readable. Off stops only the answering: the wall test still runs, and a consent wall is still `consent_required`.
settings.name: consent.handling

settings.description: What a consent wall on a domain outside `consent.domains` does: `report` (the default) leaves the page at `consent_required`, raised as `blocked`; `ask` raises a Human pause for a person's answer, for this run or always for the domain. Until the Human pause takes a person's answer, `ask` opens no page: `capability_unavailable`.
settings.name: consent.on_wall

settings.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only. An Attached engine serves no Console unless the script that starts it asks for one at an address of its own, which `hello` answers with the Console's sign-in link.
settings.name: console.address

settings.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console's content origin, which shows scraped HTML, screenshots, DOM snapshots and page bodies, as `host:port`. None by default: the Console's host on a free port, or, when `console.content_public_url` is set, the Console's own listener, which tells the two origins apart by the `Host` each request names. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.content_address

settings.description: The origin a browser reaches the Console's content origin at behind a proxy, such as `https://content.example.com`, which the addresses the Console signs name. None by default: the content origin's own listener. With no `console.content_address`, the content origin shares the Console's listener and answers the requests that name this origin's host. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.content_public_url

settings.description: Whether the Console keeps run summaries and their metadata in the browser, so that a page goes on showing them while it has no connection to the Daemon: `true`. The cache is encrypted under a key that only the sign-in's cookie unwraps, holds no secret field, and is wiped at sign-out; `false` writes nothing and wipes what an earlier page wrote. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.offline_cache

settings.description: The address links to the Console name, such as `https://console.example.com`: the links in Notifications and a run's `console_url`. None by default: the Console's own address. A link never carries a token or a cookie, so a forwarded one grants nothing. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.public_url

settings.description: How long a Console sign-in lasts without being used, in milliseconds: 30 days. Each use starts it again; a sign-in unused for longer ends, and its person signs in again. Set in an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.sign_in.idle_expiry

settings.description: How many times one address may try to sign in to the Console in a minute: 10. A further attempt in that minute is refused, whatever its credential. Set in an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.sign_in.rate

settings.description: The main-content step `page.formats` reads a page's main content with, before its Markdown, its main HTML and its text: `dom_smoothie` (the default), Readability's algorithm, or `trafilatura`, the rs-trafilatura port. A step that finds no text in a document holding text outside its navigation landmarks answers that text. Set at any scope down to a page: a Run, a Session's or a page's own `settings`.
settings.name: content.extractor

settings.description: The media types a Label's handler takes, each `type/subtype`, `type/*` or `*/*`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own list wins for its requests: `text/html` and `application/xhtml+xml` by default. A response that would reach the handler (a 2xx, or a status `crawl.handle_statuses` lists) of another type ends its request `skipped` with the reason `content_type` before its body is read, never retried. The type is the response's `Content-Type` essence, or, when it names none, the type the pinned Chromium's MIME sniffer gives its first 1,024 bytes; a response with neither a type nor a body is an empty HTML document. An accepted type that is not HTML or XHTML reaches the handler with its body in its response and a page holding no document, whose document calls fail with `response_not_document`. A handler's own navigations are not checked. A value that is no list of media ranges is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts.
settings.name: crawl.content_types

settings.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.
settings.name: crawl.domain_keys

settings.description: Statuses whose responses go to the handler as they are: a redirect status listed here is not followed, and the handler gets the 3xx as its response. None by default.
settings.name: crawl.handle_statuses

settings.description: How many work items the program's handler is given at once: 16, Scrapy's `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap at its next admission.
settings.name: crawl.handler.concurrency

settings.description: Whether a crawl's Run stays `running` with an empty Frontier and nothing in flight, waiting for new work, until `run.finish` lets it end once its work items are done: `false`, so a crawl finishes once its work items are done. Its idle time counts toward `timeout.run`, and an abort stops it as any Run.
settings.name: crawl.keep_alive

settings.description: Whether a crawl request's identity keeps its URL's fragment, so a hash-routed app's views (`#/a`, `#/b`) are separate requests, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own value wins for its requests (Crawlee's `keepUrlFragment`). Off by default: one URL with two fragments is one request. Only the tiers that run the page's scripts serve such a request: under `fetch.tier: auto` it runs on `browser`, and forcing `http`, `browser_fetch` or `discovered_api` where it is on fails the crawl's start with `setting_not_applicable`. Fixed for a Run's life: a start under the Run's ID that changes it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`.
settings.name: crawl.keep_url_fragment

settings.description: How deep a crawl goes, its seeds at depth 0 and each enqueue one level deeper than the request whose attempt added it: a deeper request is not added, with `max_depth`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.
settings.name: crawl.max_depth

settings.description: The most segments a URL's path may have, as the WHATWG parser splits it, an empty last segment (a trailing slash) not counted (Heritrix's `maxPathDepth`): a URL with more is not added, with `max_path_segments`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 20 by default; `null` turns the cap off.
settings.name: crawl.max_path_segments

settings.description: How many requests a crawl admits, its seeds included: once it admitted this many, a further one is not added, with `max_requests`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.
settings.name: crawl.max_requests

settings.description: How many times back to back a segment of a URL's path, or a run of segments, may appear (Heritrix's `maxRepetitions`), so `/a/a` passes and `/a/a/a` and `/a/b/a/b/a/b` do not, while numbers that recur apart, as in `/page/1/tag/1/sort/1`, do: a URL past it is not added, with `max_segment_repeats`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2 by default; `null` turns the cap off.
settings.name: crawl.max_segment_repeats

settings.description: How many admissions one attempt may stage before it commits: its enqueues, `enqueueLinks` calls and seeds added through `ctx.run`, each held in the engine's memory with the attempt until its commit or its discard. One more fails with `staging_full`, and nothing is staged. 10,000 by default.
settings.name: crawl.max_staged_enqueues

settings.description: The longest URL a crawl admits, in characters as the WHATWG parser serializes it, without its fragment (Scrapy's `URLLENGTH_LIMIT`): a longer one is not added, with `max_url_length`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2,083 by default; `null` turns the cap off.
settings.name: crawl.max_url_length

settings.description: Budgets for sections of a site, each a table of `pattern`, a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine against a URL's path and query, such as `/shop?*`, and `max_requests`: the first entry whose pattern a request's URL matches counts it, and once that entry counted `max_requests`, a further request it matches first is not added, with `path_budget`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`, its reasons naming the pattern and the count. A later entry the URL also matches does not count it. None by default.
settings.name: crawl.path_budgets

max_requests.description: How many requests whose URL the pattern matches first the crawl admits.

pattern.description: A glob read as Playwright reads one, such as `/shop?*`, matched in the engine against a URL's path and query.

settings.description: The longest a crawl request's Payload may be, in bytes of its JSON as the engine writes it, compactly: a longer one is refused at its enqueue with `payload_invalid`, whose `limit` names this setting, since a Payload lives in the Frontier and in every Checkpoint. Large content goes to the Key-value store, and the Payload carries its key. 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) by default.
settings.name: crawl.payload.max_size

settings.description: Whether a work item whose handler failed with `handler_failed` is tried again: `false`.
settings.name: crawl.retry.handler_failed

settings.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.
settings.name: crawl.retry.max

settings.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.
settings.name: crawl.sample_pages

settings.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, none of which a link may match, besides `crawl.scope.strategy` and `crawl.scope.include`. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.
settings.name: crawl.scope.exclude

settings.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, of which a link must match one when there are any, besides `crawl.scope.strategy`, which they never replace. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.
settings.name: crawl.scope.include

settings.description: What a crawl's links are measured by against every seed, on every enqueue, redirect and Hook rewrite: `same_hostname` (Crawlee's default), `same_domain` (the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List), `same_origin` or `all`. One leading `www.` label is ignored, and under `same_origin` an `http` seed also admits its host's `https` origin on the same port. A link outside it is not added with `out_of_scope`. Fixed for a Run's life.
settings.name: crawl.scope.strategy

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, listens, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7900 plus the major (7600 plus the minor during `0.y` previews). Port 0 takes a free port, which its log names. Only a loopback address, until the Daemon terminates TLS. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: daemon.address

settings.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.
settings.name: daemon.drain_grace

settings.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: daemon.idle_timeout

settings.description: The most rows one `dataset.query` returns; the rest are counted in its `total`, not returned. 10,000 by default.
settings.name: dataset.query.max_rows

settings.description: The most memory, in bytes, one `dataset.query` may use; past it, the query fails with `query_memory_exceeded`. 512 MiB (536870912) by default.
settings.name: dataset.query.memory_limit

settings.description: Every delivery reports its Guarantee class, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: delivery.report_guarantee_class

settings.description: Every write a Sink makes carries its delivery ID and run epoch, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: delivery.write_ids_and_epochs

settings.description: The hosts a run's requests may reach: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched on the host as a browser's URL parser leaves it (punycode, dotted-decimal IPv4), and `*` every host, only when written. `["*"]` by default; set for a connection or a Run, and only narrowed by a Recipe or a Client acting for a model, whose value listing a host the value below does not cover is `setting_locked`. A request to a host it does not list fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.allowed_domains

settings.description: The hosts no request of a run may reach, whatever `egress.allowed_domains` allows: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched as `egress.allowed_domains` matches, and `*` every host. Empty by default; set for a connection or a Run, and only added to by a Recipe or a Client acting for a model, whose value that leaves a host the value below lists uncovered is `setting_locked`. A request to a host it lists fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.blocked_domains

settings.description: The addresses a Session's connections and DNS queries leave from (ADR 0044): a list of the host's IP addresses, such as `["192.0.2.10", "2001:db8::10"]`, a network interface's name, such as `eth0`, whose addresses are read when each Session starts, or an IPv6 prefix, such as `2001:db8:1::/48`. Each Session binds one address of each IP family for its life, new Sessions spread round-robin across the blocks `egress.rotation_block.ipv4` and `.ipv6` size. A prefix covers the host's addresses inside it, and on Linux any address of it once `net.ipv6.ip_nonlocal_bind` is 1 and the prefix is routed locally. A value that yields no address the host can use refuses the run with `local_address_unavailable`, and a site with no address in a family the Session holds fails with `address_family_unavailable`. None by default: the address the OS chooses. A Recipe may expose it but never sets it, since its addresses are the machine's own.
settings.name: egress.local_addresses

oneOf.description: An interface's name, such as `eth0`, or an IPv6 prefix, such as `2001:db8:1::/48`.

settings.description: Whether Operator-configured endpoints (Model providers, Secret providers, proxies, Notification webhooks, OTLP collectors, the Plugin index, a configured `cdp_url`) are refused every address that is not globally reachable, as the addresses a page can reach are, so a tenant's endpoint never reaches the network the engine runs in. `false` by default, so an endpoint on localhost or a private network works; set only in an Operator policy, as Goodfetch Cloud sets it. A refused endpoint fails with `egress_refused` before it connects.
settings.name: egress.no_private_endpoints

settings.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: egress.offline

settings.description: The ranges and hosts that addresses a page can reach may use although they are not globally reachable, for tests against a local site or an intranet: CIDR ranges such as `127.0.0.0/8`, IP addresses, and host names, each name's connections allowed any address that is not globally reachable. A cloud-metadata address (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`) is reached only when listed by its exact address, never through a range or a host name that covers it. Empty by default; set by the program's own code, configuration or an Operator policy, by a Recipe only where the Operator policy's `egress.recipe_private_ranges` allows it, and never by a Client acting for a model, whose value is `setting_locked`. A run that lists any records it once in the Audit log as `private_addresses_allowed` and in its Run report's `weakened`.
settings.name: egress.private_ranges

items.description: A CIDR range such as `127.0.0.0/8`, an IP address such as `169.254.169.254`, or a host name such as `intranet.example`.

settings.description: Whether a Recipe may set `egress.private_ranges`. `false` by default, so a Recipe's value is `setting_locked`; set only in an Operator policy.
settings.name: egress.recipe_private_ranges

settings.description: The prefix length of the IPv4 blocks new Sessions are spread across, round-robin, when `egress.local_addresses` gives several: 24 by default, so consecutive Sessions leave from different /24 networks while the addresses allow it. Set for a connection or a Run.
settings.name: egress.rotation_block.ipv4

settings.description: The prefix length of the IPv6 blocks new Sessions are spread across, round-robin, when `egress.local_addresses` gives several: 64 by default, the block a rate limiter such as Cloudflare's counts as one client. Set for a connection or a Run.
settings.name: egress.rotation_block.ipv6

settings.description: Whether a CSV Export starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, which some spreadsheet programs need to read it as UTF-8 and which Python's `csv` module, Node's csv-parse and Unix tools read as part of the first column's name: off by default. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.csv.bom

settings.description: The one character between a CSV Export's fields: `,` by default, or such as `;` or a tab. A double quote, a carriage return, a line feed, or a text of more or less than one character fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.csv.delimiter

settings.description: How a CSV Export writes a field whose value is an object: `json`, the default, its JSON text in the field's column; `flatten`, each of its fields in a column of its own named by its dotted path, such as `author.name`, at any depth. An array, and an empty object, is its JSON text either way. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.csv.nested

settings.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's or an Atom entry's link is taken from: `url` by default; it is also the entry's ID in Atom and the item's `guid` in RSS. A Record without it gets no link, and in Atom an ID from the Run, the Dataset and its number. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.feed.link

settings.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's `pubDate` and an Atom entry's `published` and `updated` are taken from: `published` by default, read as an RFC 3339 or RFC 2822 date and time. A Record without it, or whose value is no such date, gets no date in RSS, and in Atom the time it was committed as `updated`. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.feed.published

settings.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's `description` and an Atom entry's `summary` are taken from, as text: `summary` by default. A Record without it gets none. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.feed.summary

settings.description: The field of each Record that an RSS item's or an Atom entry's title is taken from: `title` by default. A Record without it gets an empty title, or in RSS none where it has a summary. An empty text fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.feed.title

settings.description: How many spaces a JSON Export indents each level by: 0, the default, writes the array and each Record's value on one line, as committed; 1 to 8 write the array one value per line and each value's members on lines of their own, indented by that many spaces per level. JSONL is one line per Record either way. A count above 8 fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.json.indent

settings.description: The codec a Parquet Export compresses each column's pages with: `zstd`, the default, `snappy`, or `none`. It is inside the file, which every Parquet reader decodes, apart from the Export's own `compression`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.parquet.compression

settings.description: The name of an XLSX Export's one sheet: none by default, which names it after the Dataset, each character a sheet name cannot hold (`:`, `\`, `/`, `?`, `*`, `[` and `]`) written as `_` and cut to 31 characters. A name that is empty, longer than 31 characters, holds one of those characters, or starts or ends with `'` fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.xlsx.sheet

settings.description: The name of the element an XML Export writes each Record in: `record` by default. A text that is no XML name without a colon (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `-`, `.` and `_`) fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.xml.record

settings.description: The name of an XML Export's root element, which holds one element per Record: `records` by default. A text that is no XML name without a colon (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `-`, `.` and `_`) fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.
settings.name: export.xml.root

settings.description: Whether identical GET or HEAD crawl requests in flight at once from one Session, from work items that declare no Effect, wait for one response: the same method, URL, headers and body. Never across Sessions or runs, never for a Paid fetch; Provenance records each response shared. On by default.
settings.name: fetch.coalesce

settings.description: The encoding forced on each crawl request's own document after its BOM, a WHATWG Encoding label such as `shift_jis`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels; none by default. It stands where ADR 0119's order puts it: after the BOM, before the `Content-Type` charset, the `<meta>` prescan and UTF-8. It applies to the request's own document on every attempt, not to a handler's own navigations. A value that is no Encoding label is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts.
settings.name: fetch.encoding

settings.description: Whether the HTTP tier hedges a crawl request: once a GET or HEAD from a work item that declares no Effect has not answered within its route's 95th-percentile latency, a second copy is sent on a new connection through the Session's own exit, and the first answer wins, the other cancelled. Both copies hold per-domain slots and count in Usage; a Paid fetch is never hedged. Off by default; a crawl that switches it on while `politeness.domain.concurrency` is 1 is refused with `setting_not_applicable`.
settings.name: fetch.hedge.enabled

settings.description: The most hedges a run sends, as a whole percentage of the crawl requests its HTTP tier sent: 5 by default.
settings.name: fetch.hedge.max_percent

settings.description: URL patterns, each a glob or a regular expression matched in the engine, naming the responses of a crawl request's own navigation kept for its handler's `keptResponse` and `keptResponses`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own list wins for its requests. None by default: nothing is kept. Only a tier that runs the page's scripts, or `discovered_api`, can keep them: forcing `http` or `browser_fetch` where a list is set fails the crawl's start with `setting_not_applicable`; any other list set is refused at the start with `capability_unavailable` until the engine keeps responses.
settings.name: fetch.kept_responses.urls

settings.description: Whether a crawl may fetch on the `light_browser` tier: Lightpanda, run out of process, its build downloaded on first use into the Browser cache with its pinned digest and never bundled, so its AGPL licence stays outside the distribution. It runs the page's scripts without layout, and its page is the document they leave, so a wait for scripted content is served from it while a call that needs layout, pixels, a script of the handler's or a navigation escalates under `auto` and fails with `browser_required` under a forced tier. Set for the Run only. Off by default: `fetch.tier: light_browser` then fails the crawl's start with `capability_unavailable` naming this key, as it does on a platform Lightpanda builds nothing for.
settings.name: fetch.light_browser

settings.description: How many redirects a crawl request's fetch follows, a refresh stub's hop counted as one: 19 by default, as many as the browser follows in a navigation, from 1 to 19; any other value is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts. One more fails the request with `too_many_redirects`, so a redirect loop costs a site this many requests and one more. To hand a redirect to the handler unfollowed, list its status in `crawl.handle_statuses`.
settings.name: fetch.redirect.max

settings.description: The longest delay of a refresh stub a crawl request's fetch follows: a `Refresh` header, or a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` outside `<noscript>`, to another URL with a delay up to this is followed at once as one more hop, counted in `fetch.redirect.max`. 100 s by default; `0` follows instant refreshes only, and `null` any delay. A refresh with no URL or to the document's own is never followed.
settings.name: fetch.refresh.max_delay

settings.description: How many of a Label's first requests on a domain are samples under `fetch.tier: auto`, each fetched on `http` and then on `browser`, whose run commits: the Label moves to `http` once all of them gave the same Records and enqueues. 3 by default; set for the Run only. Fewer than 3 is a weakened control, named in the Run report's `weakened`.
settings.name: fetch.sample.count

settings.description: When a Label's tier choice on a domain under `fetch.tier: auto` is sampled again: after it served `requests` crawl requests, or `after` milliseconds after it was made, whichever comes first; 500 requests or 24 hours (86,400,000 ms) by default. Set for the Run only. A Label whose browser sample showed a consent wall stays on `browser` and is not sampled again.
settings.name: fetch.sample.refresh_after

after.description: The milliseconds a Label's tier choice on a domain stands before it is sampled again.

requests.description: The requests a Label's tier choice on a domain serves before it is sampled again.

settings.description: The tier that fetches each crawl request's document, set for the Run or for one of its Labels: `auto` (the default) lets the engine choose: set for the Run or a Label, it learns the tier per Label on each domain by sample comparison, the first `fetch.sample.count` requests (3) of a Label on a domain each run on `http` and then on `browser`, whose run commits, the Label moving to `http` once all of them staged the same Records (compared after Unicode NFC and whitespace normalization of their strings, in any order) and the same enqueues, the browser's run never matching where it ended on another URL or read its document in another `document.characterSet`, and staying on `browser` for the Run where its browser sample met a consent wall; split by the first segment of its URL paths when its samples disagree by segment (a segment whose own samples disagree stays on `browser`; at most 16 segments per Label and domain, the rest on `browser`), and on `browser` otherwise; a choice is sampled again as `fetch.sample.refresh_after` says; the choice is kept in the run file, so a resumed crawl takes it again, and Provenance records each attempt's tier and whether it was forced; a request on `http` escalates to the browser at the first call that tier cannot serve exactly; left at the built-in default it still gives the handler its request alone; `http` and `browser` force those tiers, nothing escalating, and a call the forced tier cannot serve fails with `browser_required`; `light_browser` forces the Lightpanda tier where `fetch.light_browser` allows it, and under `auto` a Run that allows it also runs a sample on `light_browser` where its `http` run differed, the Label moving to `light_browser` once every sample matched there or over `http`; under `auto`, a sample whose `http` run escalated at a network wait also runs on `discovered_api` once its browser run answered: the JSON calls the browser's page made, read as a page-number or cursor plan, are replayed over HTTP for the same request, a `page.wait_for_response` armed before a navigation of its page answered from the calls that navigation replays and any other escalating, and a Label whose samples all matched there, or over `http`, moves to `discovered_api`, its later requests replaying the plan for their own pages; `browser_fetch` forces the HTTP tier sent from inside the Session's browser context, its TLS fingerprint and cookies the Session's, nothing escalating; forcing `discovered_api` is refused with `capability_unavailable` at the crawl's start until a forced tier takes its browser sample.
settings.name: fetch.tier

settings.description: Whether a crawl request races its tiers: browser-fetch first, then the navigation after the Label-on-domain's median browser-fetch latency, the first result that passes the Page check and the Label's comparison winning, both counting in Politeness and Usage. The loser is cancelled, and Provenance records the race. A race does not feed the sample comparison, so a request whose Label on its domain is due a sample takes the sample instead, and a request a hidden link reached races with no navigation. Set for the Run only: a Label setting it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`, as is a Run switching it on while `politeness.domain.concurrency` is 1, where the navigation could never start. Off by default.
settings.name: fetch.tier_race

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks ads by EasyList, as a blocker does: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.
settings.name: filter_lists.ads

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks page annoyances (social widgets, newsletter and notification prompts) by Fanboy Annoyance, its cookie sections left to the Consent prompt runner: on by default in every Access mode.
settings.name: filter_lists.annoyances

settings.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.
settings.name: filter_lists.extra

settings.description: Whether a site's own scripts load whatever the Filter lists say: off by default.
settings.name: filter_lists.first_party_scripts

settings.description: Whether the Filter lists' scriptlets that patch a page's JavaScript run, from uBlock Origin's resources downloaded with the lists that name them: off by default, since a site can see them.
settings.name: filter_lists.page_scriptlets

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks trackers by EasyPrivacy: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.
settings.name: filter_lists.trackers

settings.description: How many of a Run's Sessions share one browser process, each in a browser context of its own: 8. The Run's next Session past it gets a process of its own; Sessions of different Runs never share one.
settings.name: governor.browser.contexts_per_process

settings.description: The memory, in bytes, of a browser and its processes past which it is recycled; unset by default, when the cap is twice what the browser used once it had opened its first page.
settings.name: governor.browser.memory_cap

settings.description: The memory, in bytes, of one page's JavaScript heap and the buffers it holds, past which the Resource governor ends the page while memory is critical: 1 GiB. The page ends at its safe point, once no call on it is in flight, and its calls raise `page_memory_exceeded`, which is retryable.
settings.name: governor.browser.page_memory_cap

settings.description: How long a browser may hold no open page before it closes, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage for the browser that replaces it: 5 minutes.
settings.name: governor.browser.recycle_idle

settings.description: How many pages a browser opens before it is recycled: 100. Recycled, it opens no new page, closes once its pages are done and is replaced, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage.
settings.name: governor.browser.recycle_pages

settings.description: The most browser pages the engine's Resource governor admits open at once, across its Runs: 32.
settings.name: governor.browser_page.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest browser pages the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.browser_page.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.browser_page.floor

settings.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine's memory is critical: 95.
settings.name: governor.critical

settings.description: The most HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 200.
settings.name: governor.http.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.http.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.http.floor

settings.description: How long the engine's memory may stay critical with its concurrency at the floor before the Resource governor reaches its last resort, when a Daemon's `/readyz` fails: 60 s.
settings.name: governor.last_resort_after

settings.description: The most memory, in bytes, the engine and its children may use, as its Memory allowance when it is tighter than the process's own cgroup limit, its Windows Job object's limit or half of physical memory; unset by default. Read again at every sample.
settings.name: governor.memory_allowance

settings.description: The most model calls the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 16.
settings.name: governor.model_call.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest model calls the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.model_call.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.model_call.floor

settings.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine is under pressure and its Resource governor lowers its concurrency; also the CPU and Tokio workers' busy share from which they hold it: 85.
settings.name: governor.pressure

settings.description: The share, in percent, of each kind's concurrency one Run may hold at once, at least one: 100. An Operator policy cap bounds every Run's share.
settings.name: governor.run_share

settings.description: How often the engine's Resource governor reads memory, CPU and Tokio saturation, sizes its concurrency and sends `engine.system_info`: every second.
settings.name: governor.sample_interval

settings.description: Whether a Session's pages hide, on the live page, the elements the Filter lists' cosmetic rules match: `auto` (the default) and `always` hide them through a style sheet the site cannot see on Chromium, in every frame and every new document; `off` leaves the live page as served. When the guard finds an action's target hidden, it lifts the rule for the Session and acts. Extracted content has the elements removed whatever this says.
settings.name: live_view.hiding

settings.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. A process other than the Daemon writes a set of files of its own, and at its start keeps as many of its executable's sets, its own included, the ones written last. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.file.max_files

settings.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.file.max_size

settings.description: How an engine process writes its logs on stderr, or on stdout under `daemon run`: `text`, lines for a person reading a terminal, or `json`, JSON lines. Unset, the logs are text on stderr and JSON lines on stdout under `daemon run`; a log file holds JSON lines whatever it says. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.format

settings.description: Which of its logs an engine process writes: `info`, the default, which logs state changes only (a Run started, resumed or stopped, a domain backing off, a storage level changing, a Daemon draining) and never one line per request, or any `tracing` filter directive, such as `warn` or `info,goodfetch::rpc=debug`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.level

settings.description: Where an engine process writes its logs beside stderr: `stdout`, JSON lines for the platform to collect and rotate, `file`, JSON lines in its own files of the Goodfetch home's log folder, rotated at `log.file.max_size` and kept to `log.file.max_files`, or `none`. Unset, it is `stdout` under `daemon run`, `file` for every other Daemon and `none` for an Attached engine, whose logs go to its Client as log events; `stdout` on an Attached engine, whose stdout is its protocol, fails with `setting_not_applicable`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.output

settings.description: The most decoded bytes of one body the engine itself reads: a page `request`'s response, a kept response, an Operator-configured endpoint's reply. Never a download, which the disk governor bounds. 64 MiB (67108864) by default; set for a connection or a Run. A longer body fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.
settings.name: network.max_body_size

settings.description: The most decoded bytes per received byte of a body the engine reads, once its decoded bytes pass 1 MiB, so a decompression bomb is stopped as it expands. 100 by default; set for a connection or a Run. A body past it fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.
settings.name: network.max_decompression_ratio

settings.description: The deepest nesting of arrays and objects in JSON the engine parses from outside, from 0 to 1024: 128 by default; set for a connection or a Run. Deeper JSON fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.
settings.name: network.max_json_depth

settings.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: network.resolve

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, serves its ops listener, as `host:port`: `/livez` and `/readyz` answer a status and no body to anyone, and `/metrics`, Prometheus' text, only with the ops token, the `ops.token` file of the major's folder, as a bearer token. Unset by default: no ops listener and no Prometheus export. Any address, so a cluster's probes and scrapers reach it; a request whose `Host` is a name other than `localhost`, or that carries an `Origin`, is refused. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_OPS_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: ops.address

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process sends its OpenTelemetry events to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/logs`: today the Audit log's entries, while `audit.otlp` is on. Unset, the default, sends nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: otlp.logs_endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, exports its metrics to, in protobuf, every 60 seconds and once more as it exits: a full URL such as `http://collector:4318/v1/metrics`. Unset by default: nothing is exported (ADR 0043).
settings.name: otlp.metrics_endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process exports its `tracing` spans to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`; unset, the default, exports nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. The spans cover each run, page and CDP command, with glossary IDs and bounded values as fields and a URL as its origin. Span names, span fields and the engine's targets are Experimental: a minor may change them, and its release notes list the change. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: otlp.traces_endpoint

settings.description: The RPC endpoint of each chain whose finalized state proves a payment did not settle, by chain. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: paid_fetch.chain_rpc_endpoints

settings.description: The registrable domains a run may pay for a page; `*` only when written. Widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer; a Recipe or a run only narrows it.
settings.name: paid_fetch.domains

settings.description: The fixed rates that convert a price into a Limit's currency, by currency pair. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: paid_fetch.exchange_rates

settings.description: The most a run pays for one page, as an amount and its currency such as `0.05 USD`; none by default. Raised only in configuration; a Recipe or a run only lowers it.
settings.name: paid_fetch.max_price_per_page

settings.description: Whether a domain that answers 429, 502, 503 or 504, or does not answer in time, is backed off, and its `Retry-After` waited out, for every run of the user that shares Politeness. Off, the run ignores both, and it is listed in the run's result.
settings.name: politeness.backoff.enabled

settings.description: The shortest wait of a domain's backoff: each wait is drawn at random between it and three times the previous wait (the first between it and three times it), never above `politeness.backoff.max`: 2 s. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.
settings.name: politeness.backoff.initial

settings.description: The longest wait of a domain's backoff: 60 s. A `Retry-After` may hold the domain longer, up to `politeness.retry_after.max`. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.
settings.name: politeness.backoff.max

settings.description: Whether a domain key's delay between request starts lengthens as its responses slow: on, the delay is the longer of `politeness.domain.delay` and the exponentially weighted mean (weight 0.3) of the latency of its last responses on the `http` tier, that mean capped at `politeness.backoff.max`. It only lengthens the delay, never below `politeness.domain.delay`. Off by default.
settings.name: politeness.domain.adaptive_delay

settings.description: How many crawl requests may start at once on one domain key under `politeness.domain.rate`, the size of its token bucket: 1 by default, so the starts are spread evenly over the minute. A value of 0 is read as 1.
settings.name: politeness.domain.burst

settings.description: How many requests may be in flight at once on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness: a run admits one only while that combined count is below its own value. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1. A value above 1 is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.
settings.name: politeness.domain.concurrency

settings.description: How long a run waits after the last request start on a domain key, by any run of the user that shares Politeness, before it starts another there. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1 s. A value below 1 s is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.
settings.name: politeness.domain.delay

settings.description: How many crawl requests a minute may start on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, as a token bucket of `politeness.domain.burst` tokens refilled at this rate: 30 holds a site to 30 requests a minute. Each run is held to its own value; the delay between starts still applies. None by default.
settings.name: politeness.domain.rate

settings.description: How many page navigations may be in flight at once through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run sends one only while that combined count is below its own value and below the ceiling the proxy's own refusals taught. At least 1; none by default, for no cap.
settings.name: politeness.proxy.concurrency

settings.description: How many page navigations a second may start through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run starts one only once a second divided by its own value has passed since the last start there by any sharing run. None by default.
settings.name: politeness.proxy.rate

settings.description: The longest a crawl waits for the time a site's `Retry-After` asks, past `politeness.backoff.max`: 15 minutes. When the site asks for longer, nothing is sent to its domain before that time and nothing waits for it: the request whose response asked, and each request admitted to the domain meanwhile, ends `failed` with `response_unavailable`, and `run.retry_failed` re-admits them once the site is back. Whatever its value, nothing is sent sooner than the site asked.
settings.name: politeness.retry_after.max

settings.description: How a Run shares Politeness with the other runs of its user: `shared` with every engine of the user (through the Politeness store when one is configured, else on the machine), `per_daemon` on the machine only, ignoring a store, or `run` for Politeness of its own. Anything but `shared` is listed in the Run's result.
settings.name: politeness.sharing

settings.description: The hosts the Session reaches without its proxy, as Playwright's `bypass`: a comma-separated list such as `.example.com, chromium.org`, a leading dot naming a domain's subdomains. None by default: every request goes through `proxy.server`. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.bypass

settings.description: The country, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `US`, a Session's proxy exit is in. None by default: any country the provider offers. A country the provider does not offer for the Session's proxy kind is refused with `setting_invalid` when the Session opens. A Recipe never sets it (`setting_locked`).
settings.name: proxy.country

value.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `US`.

settings.description: The proxy kind a Session's proxy is drawn from, `datacenter`, `isp`, `residential` or `mobile`: the provider's default when unset, for `list` the kind of its first server. A kind the provider does not offer is refused with `setting_invalid` when the Session opens. A Recipe may set it; a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`, since the kinds' prices differ by an order of magnitude and the person pays.
settings.name: proxy.kind

settings.description: The Secret reference of the password the Session gives `proxy.server` with `proxy.username`, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`: never a value, resolved when the Session opens and never written to a log, a trace, a process's arguments or a file. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.password

settings.description: The Proxy provider each Session of the Run, or the Session it is set on, draws its one proxy from when it opens, fixed for the Session's life: `bright_data`, `oxylabs` or `apify`, whose adapters build the provider's sticky-session username from the account in `proxy.providers.<name>` and ask for the provider's longest sticky lifetime, or `list`, the user's own servers in `proxy.providers.list.servers`. None by default. A Session that resolves both `proxy.server` and `proxy.provider` is refused with `setting_invalid`. Set as `proxy.server` is: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`.
settings.name: proxy.provider

settings.description: What each Proxy provider takes, by name, such as `proxy.providers.list`: `username`, the account's; `password`, a Secret reference resolved when a Session opens; `endpoint`, the provider's proxy URL in place of its public one (`http://brd.superproxy.io:33335` for `bright_data`, `http://pr.oxylabs.io:7777` for `oxylabs`, `http://proxy.apify.com:8000` for `apify`), an `http://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL, never `https://`, which the Session's loopback relay speaks no TLS to; `servers`, for `list` only, the user's own proxies, each a table of `server` (an `http://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL), `kind` and an optional `country`; `zones`, for `bright_data` only, the name of each proxy kind's zone as its customer named it, such as `{ residential = "residential_proxy1" }`, a kind it leaves out being the zone of the kind's own name, and the entry's `password` every zone's; and `price`, the price of a GB (10^9 bytes) through the provider, such as `5 USD`, which a currency Limit on `proxy_bytes` charges: under such a Limit a Session of an unpriced provider, or one priced in another currency, is refused with `setting_invalid`. Empty by default. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`, so no Client lowers a price, and so is a project configuration's entry that names a `price`, which only user configuration and an Operator policy set, since a currency Limit trusts it.
settings.name: proxy.providers

password.description: The Secret reference of the account's password, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`.

price.description: The price of a GB (10^9 bytes) through it, as an amount and its currency.

servers.description: The user's own servers, for `list` only.

zones.description: The zone of each proxy kind, for `bright_data` only: a kind left out is the zone of its own name.
