settings.description: The proxy every request of the Session goes through, as Playwright's `server`: an `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL with a host and a port, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`. None by default: the machine's own address. Set on a Run, every Session of it takes it; set in `run.new_session`'s `settings`, that Session alone; a page or a request has no proxy of its own, so the address a site sees never changes under the same cookies. A URL carrying credentials and `socks4` are refused with `setting_invalid`: give the credentials as `proxy.username` and `proxy.password`. Set only by the program's own code, configuration and an Operator policy: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`, since whoever sets it receives `proxy.password`. On Chromium, a SOCKS5 proxy's credentials go through a loopback relay the engine opens for the Session.
settings.name: proxy.server

value.description: A proxy URL, `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://`, with a host and an optional port and never credentials, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`.

settings.description: How long, in milliseconds, a Session asks its provider to keep its proxy exit: the provider's longest when unset. A Session that outlives it is named by the Run report's `proxy_exit_may_change` warning; the engine never looks the exit up. A `list` server's exit never changes.
settings.name: proxy.sticky_lifetime

settings.description: The username the Session gives `proxy.server`, as Playwright's `username`. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.username

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.
settings.name: resolver.attempt_delay

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.
settings.name: resolver.resolution_delay

settings.description: How a Run's commits reach the disk: `full`, the default, keeps every acknowledged commit through a power cut (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS); `fast` (`synchronous=NORMAL`) survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state. A Run in `fast` names it in its run report's `weakened`.
settings.name: run_state.durability

settings.description: The Secret reference of the key-encryption key that wraps each Run's data key. One set in a layer is resolved when a Run starts: a Run whose reference does not resolve is refused with `secret_unavailable`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration. By default the OS keychain's `keychain:goodfetch/run-state-key`, or, on a host with no OS keychain, the encrypted local file's `secretfile:run-state-key`, which `config explain` shows as the default it chose; the engine makes the default's item, a random 256-bit key, where it is missing when a Run first seals a field. A Run's data key is stored only wrapped by this key, so a resume, such as of a Checkpoint moved to another machine, unwraps it with the key this setting names for the resume, which a Client may send in `run.resume`'s project configuration: one that gives no value fails the resume with `secret_unavailable`, one that does not open the data key with `run_key_mismatch`. The encrypted local file, `secrets/<name>.age` in Goodfetch home encrypted with age to the X25519 identity in `secrets/identity.txt`, a file only its owner may read, protects copies and backups of the home, not the value from another process of the same user.
settings.name: run_state.key_reference

settings.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.
settings.name: run_state.layout

settings.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.
settings.name: run_state.location

settings.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.
settings.name: sample.echo_repeats

settings.description: The URL of the Secrets Manager endpoint that answers `aws-sm:` Secret references, such as a VPC endpoint's: unset, the default, the Region's public endpoint, `https://secretsmanager.<region>.amazonaws.com`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.aws_sm.endpoint

settings.description: The AWS Region, such as `eu-west-3`, whose Secrets Manager answers `aws-sm:name#key` Secret references: the engine calls `GetSecretValue` for the secret `name`, signed with the access key in its environment's `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and, for temporary credentials, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, and answers the secret's text, or its JSON object's `key`. Unset, the default, the engine's environment's `AWS_REGION`, then `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, names it; with none, an `aws-sm:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.aws_sm.region

settings.description: The URL of the Microsoft Entra ID authority that issues the access token `azure-kv:` references are read with, `https://login.microsoftonline.com` by default, or a sovereign cloud's, such as `https://login.chinacloudapi.cn`: the engine asks `<authority>/<AZURE_TENANT_ID>/oauth2/v2.0/token` for a token of the client-credentials grant. It is an Operator-configured endpoint, judged and verified as `secret_providers.azure_kv.endpoint` is. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.azure_kv.authority

settings.description: The URL of the Azure Key Vault that answers `azure-kv:vault/secret` Secret references, `{vault}` standing for the reference's vault name: `https://{vault}.vault.azure.net` by default, or a sovereign cloud's, such as `https://{vault}.vault.azure.cn`. The engine reads the secret's current version with an access token for Key Vault that Microsoft Entra ID (`secret_providers.azure_kv.authority`) issues to the service principal in its environment's `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` and `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`. With any of them unset, an `azure-kv:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.azure_kv.endpoint

settings.description: The absolute path of the Bitwarden CLI, `bw`, that answers `bw:item/field` Secret references from Bitwarden or, once `bw config server` points it there, a Vaultwarden server: the engine runs `bw get` without interaction and with its own environment, so `BW_SESSION` unlocks the vault. `field` is `password`, `username`, `totp` (the current code, never the seed), `notes`, `uri` or the name of a custom field. Unset, the default, a `bw:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.bw.command

settings.description: The URL of the Google Cloud Secret Manager API that answers `gcp-sm:project/secret/version` Secret references, `https://secretmanager.googleapis.com` by default, or a regional or Private Service Connect endpoint: the engine accesses the secret's version (`latest` for the newest) with the OAuth 2.0 access token in its environment's `GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, such as `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints, and answers its payload as text. With no token, a `gcp-sm:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.gcp_sm.endpoint

settings.description: The absolute path of the 1Password CLI, `op`, that answers `op://vault/item/field` Secret references: the engine runs `op read` with its own environment, so `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` or the desktop app's integration signs it in. Unset, the default, an `op://` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.op.command

settings.description: The URL of the HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao server that answers `vault:mount/path#field` Secret references, such as `https://vault.example.com:8200`: the engine reads `field` of the KV version 2 secret `path` in the secrets engine mounted at `mount`, with the token in its environment's `VAULT_TOKEN`, or `BAO_TOKEN`. It is an Operator-configured endpoint: reached on a private address unless `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses it, its certificate verified against Mozilla's roots and its own domain's `tls.trusted_cas`, never excepted by `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Plain `http:` is taken only for a loopback address, as a development server's. Unset, the default, a `vault:` reference fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "not_configured"`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: secret_providers.vault.address

settings.description: Secrets are given by Secret reference, never as values, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: secrets.by_reference

settings.description: The Secret references a Run resolves again at each use, such as a rotating token's. Any other reference is resolved once for each placeholder it fills and its value reused for the rest of the Run, its domain binding checked at each use; none by default.
settings.name: secrets.resolve_each_use

settings.description: Whether the run's Audit log entries are hash-chained (ADR 0016). On by default; off, that run's entries are written unchained, each marked `chained: false`, which `audit verify` steps over while it verifies the chain around them; the switch itself is a chained entry, and the run says so in its report's `weakened` and in one warning.
settings.name: security.audit_chain

settings.description: Whether Chromium's renderers run in their sandbox (ADRs 0017 and 0049): the engine never passes `--no-sandbox` while it is on. On by default, except on a host whose platform allows no sandbox (AWS Lambda, Fargate, Azure Container Apps), where the engine switches it off. Only an Operator policy or configuration switches it off; a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`. Off, the renderers run unsandboxed, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.
settings.name: security.browser_sandbox

settings.description: Whether the run's state seals its secret fields with the run's data key (ADR 0015). On by default; off, they are written in the clear, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.
settings.name: security.field_encryption

settings.description: Whether every browser Session the engine launches reaches the network through the egress relay, which holds a raw CDP client or a Lent page at the network layer (ADR 0017). On by default; off, a Session with no certificate exception and no local address connects directly, held by interception alone, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning. It never removes the relay that carries certificate exceptions or local addresses.
settings.name: security.raw_cdp_egress_proxy

settings.description: Whether logs, traces and HAR files are redacted and screenshots and recordings kept as outputs are masked (ADR 0014). On by default; off lifts that guarantee for those outputs only: secrets still never reach the model, Plans, caches, the Effect journal or observations. The run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.
settings.name: security.redaction

settings.description: Whether every address a name resolves to is checked against the egress policy before a connection is made (ADR 0017). On by default; off, the domain policy alone applies, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.
settings.name: security.resolved_ip_check

settings.description: Whether the run's secret tables overwrite what they delete, SQLite's `secure_delete` (ADR 0015). On by default; off, deleted values may stay on disk until overwritten, and the run says so in its report's `weakened`, in the Audit log and in one warning.
settings.name: security.secure_delete

settings.description: The Page check every page of a Session is judged against once its navigation reached its document: `login_page` and `expected_page`, each optional and each a page match, a URL glob or regular expression, a CSS or XPath selector, or a text. A page matching its login page raises `logged_out` from the call that waited for its navigation; one matching neither, when an expected page is given, raises `page_check_failed`. None by default: the built-in detector then judges a page a login page when the navigation was redirected to a login path, or when the page shows one password field outside a login path, and Provenance marks each page it judged as weakly checked. Set at a Run, a connection or a Session's own `settings`.
settings.name: session.page_check

settings.description: How long after it opened a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3,000 s, Crawlee's `maxAgeSecs`.
settings.name: session.pool.max_age

settings.description: The error score at which a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3. A block or a failed Page check adds 1, a success takes 0.5 off, never below 0 (Crawlee's model).
settings.name: session.pool.max_error_score

settings.description: How many Sessions a crawl's Session pool keeps open at once: 100. A request goes to a new Session while the pool has room, then to one drawn among those open.
settings.name: session.pool.max_size

settings.description: How many requests one Session of a crawl's Session pool serves before it is retired: 50, Crawlee's `maxUsageCount`.
settings.name: session.pool.max_uses

settings.description: Where a Session's login comes from: exactly one kind of ADR 0056's tagged union, or none for a fresh Session. Set at a Run or a connection, it is the default of the Sessions opened beneath; opening a Session takes its own as the call's `source`, and in that Session's own `settings` it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.
settings.name: session.source

settings.description: The longest robots.txt Crawl-delay a crawl waits out between request starts on a domain key while `site_preferences.respect_robots_txt` is on: 30 s. A host asking for more has its crawl requests skipped with `crawl_delay`, and its delay is not raised.
settings.name: site_preferences.max_crawl_delay

settings.description: What the run's results are for, against which the AI-use signals are judged while `site_preferences.respect_use_signals` is on: `search` (the default, which no signal is judged against), `ai-input` (input to an AI model), `ai-train` (training an AI model) or `collect` (plain collection, text and data mining).
settings.name: site_preferences.purpose

settings.description: Whether every crawl request, start URLs and sitemap entries included, and every navigation a handler makes, obeys the site's robots.txt (RFC 9309): a request it disallows, or one waiting on a robots.txt that answers 429 or 5xx or no answer, with no earlier copy, until its retries ran out, ends `skipped` with `robots_txt` and its handler never runs. On by default. Off, robots.txt is read but not obeyed, and it is listed in the run's result as a value that presses a site harder.
settings.name: site_preferences.respect_robots_txt

settings.description: Whether the AI-use signals a site sends (IETF aipref's `Content-Usage` header, TDMRep's `tdm-reservation` header) are applied to the run's `site_preferences.purpose`: on, a crawl request whose response's signal refuses the Purpose ends `skipped` with `use_signals` and its handler never runs. Off by default; the signals are read either way.
settings.name: site_preferences.respect_use_signals

settings.description: The operator's own robots.txt product token, letters, `_` and `-`: a crawl obeys the robots.txt groups naming it merged with those naming `goodfetch-foxhound`, each matched as a whole token in any case, and the `*` group only when neither has one. None by default. A value is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.
settings.name: site_preferences.robots_txt_user_agent

settings.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `critical` storage level: every Run with an essential write on it stops resumably at its next safe point, with `resource: "storage"`, and a new Run whose run file would go there is refused with `resources_exhausted`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 1 GiB and 2 % of its size, and free inodes go by 2 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: storage.critical_free

settings.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `low` storage level: its Runs go on, record no Run trace video, store no new Response cache entry, skip their periodic Checkpoints onto it, and carry the warning `storage_low`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 5 GiB and 10 % of its size, and free inodes go by 10 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: storage.low_free

settings.description: How long a locator action waits for its target to be unique and actionable, and replays a gesture that landed elsewhere, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, or `target_not_unique` for a target still ambiguous: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.action

settings.description: How long a stop of a Run, `run.stop` or a scope's close, waits for its next safe point before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, the Run still stopping there: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.close

settings.description: How long one `dataset.query` may run before it is stopped and fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.dataset_query

settings.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.first_byte

settings.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.
settings.name: timeout.handler

settings.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.
settings.name: timeout.navigation

settings.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

settings.description: How long a Secret provider may take to answer one reference before the resolution fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "timed_out"`: 30 s. A provider that answers it is briefly busy, such as a rate limit's, is asked again within it, with exponential backoff and full jitter, after its `Retry-After` when it gave one.
settings.name: timeout.secret

settings.description: How long a wait for an application state, such as `page.wait_for_request_finished`, may take before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.wait

settings.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.
settings.name: tls.accept_invalid_certs

settings.description: Client certificates for mutual TLS by domain: a host or a registrable domain with its subdomains, mapped to a table of `certificate`, the file of the certificate and its chain (PEM or DER), and `key`, the Secret reference of its private key, such as `env:CLIENT_KEY`, resolved only when a handshake with a host of that domain starts; a key given as a value is refused with `setting_invalid`. The certificate goes to the domain's hosts and nowhere else, and never to a host reached through an exception of `tls.accept_invalid_certs`. Set from every layer, a Recipe and a run included; nothing is installed on the machine.
settings.name: tls.client_certificates

certificate.description: The file of the client certificate and its chain, PEM or DER.

key.description: The Secret reference of the certificate's private key, such as `env:CLIENT_KEY`, resolved at the handshake.

settings.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: a host or a registrable domain with its subdomains, mapped to certificate files or Secret references, trusted beside the default roots for that domain and nowhere else. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run; on a Daemon with accounts only the operator role writes it, in the Operator policy.
settings.name: tls.trusted_cas

settings.description: Whether an executable more than three months past its release date prints one line a day on stderr saying so, from its own release date alone, with no network call. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

settings.description: The domains whose Walls no run reads past, whatever another layer allows. Set only in an Operator policy.

settings.description: The domains whose Walls a run may read past by generic means. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.

settings.description: The domains on which reading past a Wall may fetch a page again. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration, never by an answer.
